description: Novel optics and AI approaches to image the centre of a live root for the first time. This exciting opportunity is based within the thriving Optics and Photonics Research Group in Faculty of Engineering which conducts cutting edge research spanning exploration to translation, with curiosity driven projects all the way through to application in the clinic. Vision We are seeking PhD student that is motivated and enthusiastic and keen to push the boundaries of what is currently possible when imaging with an optical microscope. Combing the latest in optical developments with the recent surge in AI, this project aims image the centre of a live intact root for the first time. Something that is currently not possible. Motivation This project will address a long-standing issue in plant biology: the inability to image the centre of live, intact, plant roots. The ability to observe dynamic cellular processes at the centre of a live root for the first time will unlock entirely new lines of biological inquiry, crucial for areas such as sustainable agriculture and food security. Such an imaging system would allow for studies of a plant’s resilience to drought, salinity, and water logging, as well as responses to fungal infections and nanoparticle uptake. It is very common that new optical microscopy techniques are developed to image mammalian tissue, and that these approaches are very slow to translate across to plant biosciences where the impact could be huge and as a result exciting opportunities get missed. When we use light to image deep into complex samples there is a common problem that occurs – the light gets distorted and scattered by the structures present in the sample and as a result a nice quality focus and hence a nice image cannot be produced at depth into the sample. At Nottingham we have been working on this problem for several years and have developed methods that shape the incoming light with the equal but opposite distortion to that imposed by the sample to produce a high-quality image deep into the sample of interest. Recently we have been using AI and machine learning to predict the distortion present and significantly speed up this correction process. This PhD project will take the latest in AI-informed wavefront correction techniques and tailor them to imaging deep into plant roots. It will use a range of state-of-the-art optical microscopes based in the Optics and Photonics Research Group in the Faculty of Engineering, plus those housed in Plant Biosciences at the Sutton Bonnington campus. Data sets will be generated using simulated and experimental data and these will be used to train networks to predict the common distortions that occur when imaging into plant roots. From here we can either correct for these distortions using the hardware in the microscope or in software using reconstruction algorithms. This is an exciting multidisciplinary PhD project that promises to make cutting-edge advances in all research areas involved. Aim This project combines practical hands-on optics experimentation with training neural networks to develop the next generation of optical microscopes. You will have the opportunity gain skills in optical instrumentation and imaging, AI and machine learning, and in plant biology and sample handling. Your base will be in the Optics and Photonics Group in the Faculty of Engineering and from here you will work with a team of academics and researchers across Engineering, Computer Science and the Biosciences. You will be supervised by Amanda Wright (Optics and Photonics Research Group, Faculty of Engineering), Mike Somekh (Optics and Photonics Research Group, Faculty of Engineering), Mike Pound (Computer Vision, Computer Science Department), and Darren Wells (Plant and Crop Biophysics, School of Biosciences). Who we are looking for An enthusiastic, self-motivated, resourceful student, who likes working as part of a team and is keen to take on a new challenge. An understanding of optics and/or machine learning is desirable but not essential, along with general coding skills. 1 st or a 2:1 in a relevant field (for example Physics, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Computer Science, or Biosciences). Funding support After a suitable candidate is found, funding is then sought from the University of Nottingham as part of a competitive process (this will cover home tuition fees and UKRI stipend) The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The Faculty of Engineering provides a thriving working environment for all PGRs creating a strong sense of community across research disciplines. Community and research culture is important to our PGRs and the FoE support this by working closely with our Postgraduate Research Society (PGES) and our PGR Research Group Reps to enhance the research environment for PGRs. PGRs benefit from training through the Researcher Academy’s Training Programme, those based within the Faculty of Engineering have access to bespoke courses developed for Engineering PGRs. including sessions on paper writing, networking and career development after the PhD. The Faculty has outstanding facilities and works in partnership with leading industrial partners. Please contact Amanda Wright with your CV and supporting statement to apply for this project – amanda.wright@nottingham.ac.uk Closing Date: 02 Feb 2026 Category: Studentships

description: 3.7K Application Deadline: 8 October 2026 23:59. Applications are now open for the 2027 France–South Africa Scholarship Programme. The France-South Africa Scholarship Programme is directed to students who intend to study in universities or higher education institutions in France for their Master’s degree or PhD. The programme is open to students with citizenship of South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi. Requirements This call for applications is open to all fields of study. Priority will be given to applications in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields, including related humanities and social sciences disciplines. Eligible study programmes The France–South Africa Scholarship Programme supports studies at Master’s and PhD level in French higher education institutions located in France. Joint or international degree programmes are eligible, provided that at least one of the partner institutions is located in France. However, scholarship funding will only cover the period of study and research undertaken in France. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that their chosen programme leads to a qualification officially recognised by the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research. As the South African Qualifications Authority (SAQA) only evaluates qualifications once studies have been completed, it is important to verify the status of the qualification before applying. Please note that many programmes labelled as Master of Science (MSc) are not nationally recognised Master’s degrees in France unless explicitly stated otherwise. Applicants should therefore carefully check the accreditation and recognition status of their chosen programme. General requirements To be eligible for the France-South Africa Scholarship Programme, applicants must be: Born on or after 1 January 1997. A citizen of South Africa, Lesotho or Malawi. Dual French citizens are not eligible. Have achieved a minimum average of 60% in their most recently completed degree. For Master’s applicants: plan to enrol in a French higher education institution to pursue a Master’s degree. Applicants are not required to have secured admission at the time of submitting their scholarship application. For PhD applicants: plan to pursue a PhD at a French higher education institution and have identified a prospective supervisor or research laboratory in France. Applicants are not required to have a formal admission offer at the time of submitting their scholarship application. Scholarship Worth France Excellence scholarship holder status, includes: – Social security coverage and health insurance; – Priority access to student housing; – Exemption from visa fees; – Support services provided by Campus France Paris; – Exemption from the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC); – Conditional exemption from registration fees for programmes offered by public universities under the supervision of the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research, provided that no additional tuition fees apply. – One return flight ticket between the recipient’s country of residence and France. – A monthly living allowance (900€ per month for Master’s students and 1850€ per month for PhD students, subject to reassessment). – Eligibility to apply for additional housing support from the French Family Allowance Fund (CAF), which may provide approximately 150€ per month depending on individual circumstances. Please note that tuition fees are not covered by the scholarship. Applicants are therefore encouraged to consider tuition costs when selecting a programme. Scholarship holders are exempt from tuition fees at public higher education institutions that apply the standard national tuition rates for non-European students. Applicants who require assistance identifying suitable programmes may contact Campus France for guidance. Applicants may seek additional funding from other sources to help cover these expenses and must inform the Embassy of France if they obtain any additional funding. Application Timeline: Applications open: 21 July 2026 Application deadline: 8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa time) Information webinar: August 2026 (follow Campus France South Africa on social media for details) Interviews for eligible candidates: November 2026 Announcement of shortlisted candidates: Beginning of December 2026 French language courses: February–July 2027 Departure to France and start of studies: September 2027 For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the France–South Africa Scholarship Programme

description: 602 Application Deadline: 20 October , 2026 Applications are now open for the 2027/2028 Commonwealth PhD Scholarships. The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC) provides the UK government scholarship scheme led by international development objectives. It operates within the framework of the Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan (CSFP) and offers a vivid demonstration of the UK’s enduring commitment to the Commonwealth. By attracting individuals with outstanding talent and identifiable potential from all backgrounds and supporting them to become leaders and innovators on returning to their home countries, the CSC’s work combines sustainable development with the UK national interest and provides opportunities for international partnerships and collaboration. Purpose: Funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) , Commonwealth PhD scholarships contribute to the development needs of Commonwealth countries by supporting research that will have a developmental impact. They also enhance individual teaching and research capacity leading to increase institutional capacity in academic and other sectors in Commonwealth countries, and will contribute to UK higher education and research by attracting high-calibre international applicants and encouraging links and collaboration, and are aimed at those who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK. Intended beneficiaries: Commonwealth PhD scholarships are for high-quality graduates who have the potential to undertake world-class research of a developmental nature and to become influential leaders, teachers, or researchers in their home countries. Applicant eligibility To apply for this scholarship, applicants must: Be a citizen of or have been granted refugee status by an eligible Commonwealth country, or be a British Protected Person. Be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country. Be available to start academic studies in the UK by the start of the UK academic year in September 2027. By September 2027, hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours standard, or a lower second-class degree and a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a Master’s degree)*. Not be registered for a PhD, or an MPhil leading to a PhD, at a UK university or in their home country before September/October 2026. Be unable to afford to study in the UK without this scholarship. Have provided all supporting documentation in the required format. Each scholarship provides: Approved airfare from the Scholar’s home country to the UK and return at the end of the award (the CSC will not reimburse the cost of fares for dependants, nor the cost of journeys made before the award is confirmed). Approved tuition fees: full fees are covered by agreement between the CSC and the UK university, and Scholars are not liable to pay for any part of the tuition fee. Stipend (living allowance) at the rate of £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month for those at universities in the London metropolitan area (rates quoted at current levels). Study travel grant towards the cost of study-related travel within the UK or overseas. Provision towards the cost of fieldwork undertaken overseas (the cost of one economy class return airfare to the fieldwork location), where approved. Paid mid-term visit (airfare) to the Scholar’s home country, unless they have claimed or intend to claim spouse and/or child allowances during their scholarship or have received a return airfare to their home country for fieldwork. Family allowances, as follows (rates quoted at current levels): If a Scholar is accompanied by their spouse but no children: spouse allowance of £313 per month for a maximum period of nine months, if they and their spouse are living together at the same address in the UK (unless the spouse is also in receipt of a scholarship; other conditions also apply). If a Scholar is accompanied by their spouse and children: spouse allowance of £313 per month and child allowance of £313 per month for the first child, and £154 per month for the second and third child under the age of 16, if their spouse and children are living with them at the same address in the UK (unless their spouse is also in receipt of a scholarship; other conditions also apply). If a Scholar has children and is widowed, divorced, or a single parent, child allowance of child allowance of £622 per month for the first child, and £154 per month for the second and third child under the age of 16, if their children are living with them at the same address in the UK. How to apply Applications for Commonwealth PhD scholarships for the 2027/28 academic year will open on Tuesday 8 September . The closing date for applications to be received is 16.00 BST on Tuesday 20 October . The scholarships are for study in the UK beginning in September/October 2027. Applications to the CSC are made using the application system, CSC Central . The CSC is unable to accept any applications or documentation not submitted via CSC Central . Application Documents template application form guidance document For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the Commonwealth PhD Scholarships

description: 396 Application Deadline: 23 October 2026, 23:59 EAT (UTC+3) Applications are now open for the AU Theme of the Year 2027 Official Logo and Visual Identity Competition. The Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM), launched in 2018, is a flagship project of Agenda 2063 aimed at creating a unified and liberalised air transport market across Africa. At the same time, New technologies, including artificial intelligence, digital identity, cybersecurity, digital public infrastructure and space technologies, are transforming connectivity across the continent, guided by AU Digital Transformation Strategy (DTS 2020 – 2030). To give the Theme a distinctive, meaningful and youth-driven visual identity, the African Union Commission’s Infrastructure and Energy Department, with the support of the African Union Development Agency–NEPAD (AUDA-NEPAD), is launching a continental logo competition for young African creatives. More than a design exercise, the competition invites Africa’s youth to give visual expression to the continent’s shared aspirations. It calls on emerging creatives to capture the significance of the African Union’s 25-year journey, the promise of open and connected African skies through SAATM, the transformative potential of new technologies, and the enduring vision of a more integrated, inclusive and prosperous Africa. The selected logo will serve as the visual identity of the Theme throughout 2027, conveying its ambition and significance across the continent and beyond. It should reflect Africa’s rich diversity and shared identity while portraying a continent in motion connected through its people, infrastructure and technologies, and united by a common vision for the future. By placing young Africans at the centre of the creative process, the initiative recognises that Africa’s youth are not only beneficiaries of continental integration but also active contributors to shaping its future. Their creativity, imagination and understanding of Africa’s evolving identity will help translate this continental priority into a powerful and memorable visual expression. Objectives The logo competition aims to: Recognise and promote emerging African creative talent. Engage young Africans in shaping the public identity of a continental priority. Generate early awareness, ownership and momentum around the Theme of the Year. Translate the AU at 25, African integration, SAATM and new technologies into a clear and compelling visual concept. Reflect African Union values, Agenda 2063 and the aspirations of a connected, inclusive and prosperous Africa. Create a consistent visual identity for use by the African Union and its partners throughout 2027. Eligibility Requirements Open to citizens of all AU Member States aged 18–24 on the submission deadline Entries must be submitted by individuals (no joint/team submissions) Students, designers, artists, digital creatives, innovators welcome — formal qualifications not required One entry per applicant Members of the evaluation process, AU personnel, contractors and immediate family are not eligible Required Submission Package Completed application form (name, nationality, DOB, contact, brief profile) Proof of nationality and age Presentation PDF with primary logo, colour, B&W, reversed versions + 3 mock-ups Preview PNG/JPEG (minimum width 3000px) Concept note (≤500 words) explaining idea, symbolism, colour, adaptability Signed originality, intellectual-property and AI declaration Technical, Originality & AI Requirements Must be original, created specifically for this competition, not previously published or submitted Must not reproduce the AU emblem, existing logos, national symbols, stock or third-party material Design must remain recognisable in colour/monochrome, at small sizes, on light/dark backgrounds Wordmark must allow adaptation into AU working languages Shortlisted applicants must provide editable vector source files (SVG, EPS, .ai) within 3 working days Submission Procedure Download and read competition documents from the official webpage Prepare complete submission package in required formats Remove applicant’s name, signature, photo and social-media handle from the logo presentation (applicant info only in the application form) Submit through the official channel accessible from the competition webpage Retain the automated acknowledgement as proof Benefits USD 5,000 : First place USD 2,000 Second place USD 1,000 : Third place A certificate of recognition; Official acknowledgement through African Union platforms; and Training opportunities. The winner will also have the opportunity to participate in the AU Summit, where the winning logo will be officially unveiled. The winning concept will be refined in consultation with the applicant and in accordance with African Union branding guidelines for official use throughout 2027. Any additional recognition arrangements will be communicated on the official competition webpage. Application Process Completed application form and brief profile Proof of nationality and age Presentation PDF containing all required logo versions and three mock-ups High-resolution PNG or JPEG preview files (min 3000px) Signed originality, IP and AI declaration Applicant identity removed from the design presentation Complete package submitted through the official channel before the deadline For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the AU Theme of the Year 2027 Official Logo and Visual Identity Competition

Have the ability to perform laboratory protocols for the nutritional characterisation of food products and possess a good command of English. No Offer Description At UBC, we believe that attracting and sustaining a diverse workforce is key to the successful pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning for all faculty, staff and students. Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career. The Department of Medicine and the School of Biomedical Engineering at The University of British Columbia (UBC) invites applications for a Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader in Global Health Engineering and Equitable Health Technologies, addressing the Impact+ strategic priority area of Health, including Biotechnology. The successful candidate will be appointed to a tenure-track faculty position and the home department will be the Department of Medicine. The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program is a one-time initiative designed to support institutions in attracting internationally based Early Career Researchers to Canada. Emerging Leaders will receive research funding and institutional supports to advance transformative research in Canada’s strategic priority areas, build partnerships across sectors and borders, and translate their research into applications and impacts that benefit Canadians and the world. Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders are six-year positions valued at $100,000 annually, renewable once for an additional six years, intended for exceptional emerging scholars who have the potential to lead in their fields. Applicants must be early-career researchers and be eligible to hold a full-time, tenure-stream appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor at UBC. Under the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program, nominees must be working and residing outside Canada when the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada award ( https://www.canada.ca/en/impact-plus-chairs.html ) is formally accepted (July 1st 2026). Applicants may apply regardless of their current location; however, candidates selected for nomination must meet this eligibility requirement on the award acceptance date in order to proceed. Expatriate Canadians wishing to relocate to Canada are welcome to apply. The UBC Department of Medicine provides excellence in research, teaching and clinical services related to the nature, cause, prevention, and treatment of adult diseases. As the largest department in the Faculty of Medicine, comprised of eighteen Divisions, and over twelve hundred faculty and staff located throughout the Province of British Columbia, the Department of Medicine is committed to ensuring the success of learners and faculty, and to contributing to the health of the Province of British Columbia. The School of Biomedical Engineering (SBME) is a partnership between the Faculties of Applied Science and Medicine, established in 2017. The School is a nucleus for education and training, research, and innovation in biomedical engineering, creating new knowledge, new academic and training programs, and fostering translation and innovation. Its vision is to transform health and healthcare for all, achieved through innovative research and education at the convergence of engineering, medicine and biology. Through collaborative, innovative, and interdisciplinary approaches and building on UBC’s academic and research excellence, the School of Biomedical Engineering aspires to be a global leader in biomedical engineering research, education and translation. The SBME has two locations on Vancouver’s campus, the Gordon B Shrum building and the Biomedical Research Centre (BRC). For more information about the School of Biomedical Engineering, please visit https://www.bme.ubc.ca/ . Key Expectations of the Position Reporting jointly to the Head of the UBC Department of Medicine and the Director of the UBC School of Biomedical Engineering, the successful candidate will establish and lead a research program in Global Health Engineering and Equitable Health Technologies. Consistent with the broad goals of global health, namely improving health and achieving health equity for all populations, the position seeks individuals who apply engineering, technology, and innovation to address important health challenges and reduce inequities in health outcomes and access to care in Canada and globally. The successful candidate will be expected to: Lead a research program focused on the development, translation, implementation, and evaluation of innovative technologies that improve health outcomes and advance health equity across diverse populations, healthcare systems, and resource settings. Advance research at the intersection of engineering, health sciences, clinical medicine, public health, and health systems. Develop technologies and solutions that address unmet needs in disease prevention, diagnosis, treatment, monitoring, rehabilitation, and healthcare delivery. Pursue research in areas such as medical devices, diagnostics, biosensors, wearables, therapeutics, biotechnology-enabled innovations, digital health, artificial intelligence, data science, and other engineering- and technology-based approaches that improve health and advance health equity. Develop and evaluate technologies in partnership with healthcare providers, communities, patients, health authorities, public health organizations, and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are effective, scalable, and responsive to real-world needs. Leverage the Conconi Family Biodevice Foundry ( https://biodevicefoundry.bme.ubc.ca/ ) and other UBC research infrastructure to accelerate technology development, prototyping, validation, and deployment. Contribute to teaching activities within the Department of Medicine and the School of Biomedical Engineering, including undergraduate and graduate biomedical engineering education and interdisciplinary initiatives such as the Department of Medicine's Data Science and Health (DASH) Research Excellence Cluster. Mentor and train undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate learners. Contribute service to the Department of Medicine, the School of Biomedical Engineering, the Faculties of Medicine and Applied Science, the University, and the broader academic and professional communities. Collaborate across disciplines to advance strategic priorities in research, education, innovation, and translation. Minimum and Preferred Qualifications of Candidates Candidates must hold an MD and/or PhD, as part of the UBC requirement, and be eligible for appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor at UBC. Candidates must hold, or be eligible to obtain, registration as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) or Limited Licensee with Engineers and Geoscientists BC (EGBC). Applicants from engineering disciplines, as well as quantitatively intensive fields such as mathematics, computer science, quantitative neuroscience, physics, and related disciplines, are encouraged to apply, provided they are eligible for registration with EGBC. Information regarding Limited License eligibility is available at: https://www.egbc.ca/Registration/Individual-Registrants/How-to-Apply/Professional-Registration/Professional-Licensee. The successful candidate will demonstrate: Evidence of excellence, or strong potential for excellence, in research, teaching, mentorship, and scholarly activity. An established or emerging research program in Global Health Engineering, Equitable Health Technologies, Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, or a related field. Expertise in the development, translation, evaluation, or implementation of innovative health care technologies, such as diagnostics, biosensors, medical devices, therapeutics, vaccines, digital health platforms, or AI-enabled solutions. A commitment to advancing equitable access to healthcare through technologies that address unmet clinical and public health needs in diverse populations and resource settings. The Law Centre for Health and Life at the Amsterdam Law School is looking for a researcher to help explore this question. Join the project team! What you will do Working with the project team, you will Map EU and Dutch legal and policy rules for sharing and reusing genomic and other sensitive health data. Compare opt-in, opt-out and hybrid approaches to individual choice, and examine their implications for research, privacy, fairness and public trust. Help develop interview guides and clear scenarios for discussions with stakeholder groups. Help prepare, conduct and analyse interviews with policymakers, data stewards, researchers, and patient or community representatives. Bring the legal and interview findings together in academic writing and accessible outputs, including a decision map and policy brief. You will also be part of the Centre’s wider research community, collaborating on related health law and digital health work where it connects to your agreed responsibilities. What you bring A completed PhD in law or a related field is preferred. We will also consider applicants with a relevant master’s degree and strong research experience. The appointment level and salary scale will reflect the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience. You can carry out careful, independent research, work well with colleagues, and explain complex findings clearly to academic and wider audiences. Experience with health law, data protection, EU law, or qualitative interviews is an advantage. Excellent written and spoken English is required. Professional working proficiency in Dutch is a strong advantage. Preferably you are available on short notice (starting 1 December 2026). What do we offer? The position is for 0.5 fte and offered for 1 year. The gross full-time monthly salary will be in accordance with the salary scales for junior (post-doc) Researchers at Dutch universities, scale 10 (Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities) ranging from €3.706 to €5.760 gross per month (full-time equivalent). As mentioned before the appointment level and salary scale will reflect the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience. Secondary benefits at Dutch universities are attractive and include 8% holiday pay and an 8.3% end-of-year bonus This is where you will be working You will work primarily on two complementary projects supported by an NWO Open Competition XS award and the Amsterdam Law School’s Democratic Digital Transformation (DDT) initiative. You will be part of the project team which is based at the Law Center for Health and Life, at the Law Faculty of the University of Amsterdam (UvA). It is also a great chance to connect with peers from around the world that share a passion for IP. No Offer Description NOTICE OF OPENING OF AN INTERNATIONAL SELECTION PROCEDURE FOR THE RECRUITMENT OF A PHD STUDENT RESEARCHER AT THE FACULTY OF ENGINEERING OF THE UNIVERSITY OF PORTO - (Fixed-term employment contract of uncertain duration) By order dated 06/10/2026, of the Dean of FEUP, Professor Rui Artur Bártolo Calçada, it was decided to open an international selection procedure for one PhD student researcher position, within the scope of Project LEGEND - Leading-Edge evaluation and GENeration of Defect-tolerance in composite structures funded by the European Commission under Grant_Agreement nº 101312790 - Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks, under a fixed-term employment contract of uncertain duration, pursuant to the Labour Code, approved by Law No. 7/2009 of 12 February, as currently worded, Regulation No. 849/2026 of 07/07 - Regulation on Research, Science and Technology Staff of the University of Porto (hereinafter referred to as the Regulation), and other applicable legislation. The contract shall remain in force only for the period required to carry out the project tasks defined and identified below, with an expected duration of 36 months, and shall never exceed the maximum limit of four years. The PhD student researcher shall develop scientific research leading to the award of a PhD, as provided for in paragraph 1 of Article 20 of Regulation No. 849/2026 of 7 July. The PhD student researcher will join the team of project LEGEND, carrying out and developing the activities of DC3 of 14 DCs within LEGEND, focused on correlating mechanical performance degradation in composite materials with quantified micro-scale variabilities and defects, in accordance with the guidelines of the project Dissemination Plan, within the scientific area of Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering or related fields. In particular, the PhD student researcher will contribute to the following project activities, as set out in the application: The PhD student researcher will develop an approach to quantify how micro-scale defects and variability influence structural allowables, and create a predictive tool for these allowables as a function of the micro-structural metrics. The PhD student researcher will combine Design of Experiments-driven manufacturing and mechanical testing of composite laminates, coupled with advanced High-Resolution (HR) X-Ray imaging and Machine Learning (ML) segmentation techniques to link micro-scale defects to performance variability, improving our present understanding and predictive capabilities of the effects of such defects on the material allowables used in structural design. Expected Results : An extensive data set detailing micro-structural metrics and related allowables resulting from different manufacturing processes and materials; and an understanding of the strain rate-dependence of these allowables; a ML-based tool to predict these allowables. The primary tasks performed by the PhD student researcher will be: - Develop an efficient tool capable of predicting design allowables as a function of the micro-structural variabilities and defects in composite materials. - Develop scientific concepts and communicate the results of research through written scientific publications and oral presentations at international conferences. - Fulfil the requirements of the Doctoral Program in Mechanical Engineering to be awarded the doctoral degree: completion of 36 ECTS of mandatory (6 ECTS) and optional (30 ECTS) courses in the first year, completion of a 24 ECTS Seminar at the end of the first year, and completion of a Thesis (120 ECTS) at the end of the third year ( FEUP - Doctoral Program in Mechanical Engineering ). - Collaborate with fellow doctoral candidates within the LEGEND project, utilising synergies between projects. - Actively participate in General Assembly meetings and doctoral training events within LEGEND, distributed across Europe. Consequently, the net salary/net allowances result from deducting compulsory employee social security contributions as well as direct taxes (e.g. income tax) and any other applicable taxes/contributions. 3. Any formalities established therein must be completed by the date of recruitment. 3.2. Special admission requirements 3.2.1. For the purpose of determining the profile suited to the activity to be performed, the following are special requirements: a) candidates must have skills and previous experience in the mechanics of fibre-reinforced polymers. b) English language proficiency at level B2 as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). c) not already in possession of a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible. d) mobility rule: at the time of the recruitment candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Portugal for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date, unless as part of a compulsory national service or a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention (short stays such as holidays are not taken into account). ‘Recruitment date’ means the first day of the employment of the researcher for the purposes of the project (i.e. the starting date indicated in the employment contract). 3.2.2. No Offer Description NOTICE NO. 103/2026 COMPETITION FOR THE AWARD OF A GRANT, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROVISIONS OF THE RESEARCH GRANT REGULATIONS OF UALG Title: 1 Research Fellowship Position – Master's Degree Holder A competition is open for the award of 1 Research Fellowship Position – Master's Degree Holder within the scope of the R&D project Adaptações dos sobreiros face às alterações climáticas e como as mesmas promovem a sustentabilidade do ecossistema/ Cork Oak Adaptations to Climate Change and Their Contribution to Ecosystem Sustainability , from the University of Algarve, ALGARVE-FEDER-03316200 OAKHIMEDES, funded ICDT ALGARVE 2030), under the following conditions: Scientific Area : Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering . Admission Requirements : A master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related fields, qualifying the holder for enrollment in a doctoral program. Preferred qualifications include knowledge and experience in: data analysis, processing, and visualization, including applied statistics and exploratory data analysis; scientific programming—ideally in Python—and the use of tools and libraries for data science and artificial intelligence; machine learning, including classification methods, clustering, data mining, multivariate analysis, time-series analysis, and variable selection and interpretation; and the analysis and integration of data from environmental sensors, monitoring systems, the Internet of Things (IoT), or similar applications. Candidates should also demonstrate critical thinking, autonomy in problem-solving, an aptitude for scientific research, and the ability to integrate multidisciplinary information. Taking into account paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 6 of the Research Grants Regulations of the Foundation for Science and Technology or paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 5 of the University of the Algarve’s Research Fellowship Regulations: “1. Research grants, hereinafter referred to as BI, are intended for R&D activities by students enrolled in an integrated master's degree, a master's degree or a doctorate, with a view to consolidating their scientific training through the development of research work leading to the award of the respective academic degree, whether or not integrated into R&D projects. 2. The scholarships referred to in this article may also be intended for the performance of R&D activities by graduates or masters enrolled in non-degree courses integrated into the educational project of a higher education institution, developed in association or cooperation with one or more R&D units.” Project Objectives : Monitor weather and soil conditions at two experimental forest sites through the systematic collection of data using sensors, in order to characterize the influence of environmental factors on tree growth, physiological response, and adaptive capacity. Analyse the relationships between climatic variables, soil conditions, radial growth, and physiological parameters, identifying the environmental factors with the greatest influence on tree response, as well as potential indicators of resilience and adaptation to climate change. Develop and apply machine learning models to identify patterns in the collected data and determine which variables possess the greatest explanatory and discriminatory power. Employ exploratory data analysis and visualization methods to identify clusters, interpret their biological and environmental significance, and determine which variables carry the most weight in differentiating the physiological states of the trees. Applicable Legislation and Regulations : Research Fellow Statute, approved by Law No. 40/2004 of August 18, as amended by Decree-Law No. 65/2024 of October 1, and the University of Algarve Research Grant Regulations ( https://files.dre.pt/2s/2021/10/210000000/0013700149.pdf ). Workplace: The work will be carried out at CIMA (Centro de Investigação Marinha e Ambiental) and the ISE (Instituto Superior de Engenharia) at UAlg, under the scientific guidance of Professors Ana Cristina Hurtado de Matos Coelho, Jorge Filipe Leal Costa Semião, and Pedro Jorge Sequeira Cardoso. Duration of grant(s): The grant will last 12 months, with the start date scheduled in january of 2027. The grant contract may be renewed until the end of the project, taking into account the University of Algarve Research Grant Regulations ( https://files.dre.pt/2s/2021/10/210000000/0013700149.pdf ). Monthly maintenance allowance amount : The monthly maintenance allowance is €1359.64. The maintenance allowance will be paid monthly by bank transfer. https://www.fct.pt/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Tabela-de-Valores-SMM-202… ). Candidate evaluation : In accordance with the provisions of Article 11.2 of the Research Fellowship Regulations of the University of Algarve, candidates will be assessed based on their curriculum vitae evaluation (AC) and, only if deemed necessary by the Selection Committee, an interview (E). The evaluation of applications will be based on a combined assessment of the following criteria: C1 – Final average grade of academic qualifications: Score corresponding to the average grade of academic qualifications, rounded to the nearest whole number. Weighting: P1 = 0.2; C2 – Professional training, professional experience, and technical and scientific curriculum: Weighting: P2 = 0.4; C3 – Suitability for the research area applied for and research experience in the relevant fields: Weighting: P3 = 0.4. The curriculum vitae evaluation (AC) will be scored on a scale of 0 to 20 points, according to the following formula: AC = C1 × P1 + C2 × P2 + C3 × P3 If deemed necessary by the Selection Committee, individual interviews (E) will be conducted with the three highest-ranked candidates. In this case, the final score will be calculated according to the following formula: Final Score = AC × 0.8 + E × 0.2 Composition of the Application Evaluation Board: The Application Evaluation Board is composed of three full members and one alternate (all PhDs): Ana Cristina Hurtado de Matos Coelho (Presidente) (Professora coordenadora; Escola Superior de Educação e Comunicação); Jorge Filipe Leal Costa Semião (1º Vogal efetivo) (Professor coordenador; Instituto Superior de Engenharia); Pedro Jorge Sequeira Cardoso (2º Vogal efetivo) (Professor coordenador; Instituto Superior de Engenharia); Paulo Gustavo Martins da Silva (1º Vogal suplente) (Professor adjunto; Instituto Superior de Engenharia); Publication/Notification of Results: The final evaluation results will be published on the UAlg website, in a list ordered by the final grade obtained, and the successful candidate will be notified via email. Application Deadline and Submission Method: The competition is open from 26/10/2026 to 06/11/2026. Applications must be accompanied by the following documents: Official identification document (simple copy or legal equivalent). Applicants of non-Portuguese nationality must present a residence permit, permanent residence certificate, or long-term resident status, valid on the scholarship start date. Any of these may be replaced, in its absence, by a declaration of honor by the candidate. However, this must be submitted during the scholarship contracting phase, under penalty of forfeiture of the scholarship award; Curriculum Vitae; Copy of the qualification certificates for the academic degrees held, specifying the final grade and, if possible, the grades obtained in all courses taken; Other documents deemed relevant due to the type and modality of the scholarship. e) The Application for Application to the Competition, dated and signed, must be addressed to the President of the Competition Evaluation Panel, https://www.ualg.pt/sites/default/files/documentos/2022-12/anexo-iii-requerimento-para-candidatura-bolsa-pt.pdf , by email to acoelho@ualg.pt , and cc'd to jsemiao@ualg.pt , Ref.ª EDITAL N. º 103/2026 . In the aforementioned application, you must expressly consent to all notifications related to the bidding process being sent to the indicated email address . Documents to be submitted for the scholarship agreement: Individual Taxpayer Registry (INV) information, if the applicant is a nationality other than Portuguese, must be submitted during the scholarship agreement process, under penalty of forfeiture of the scholarship award; Documents proving that the applicant meets the requirements for the respective type of scholarship, namely, proof of enrollment and registration and the study cycle or course that does not confer an academic degree; Declaration of the advisor(s) assuming responsibility for supervising the work plan, in accordance with Article 5-A of the Research Scholarship Statute, as well as guaranteeing the necessary conditions for the successful development of the work and compliance with the duties set forth in Article 13 of the Research Scholarship Statute; d. Declaration of Commitment to the Exclusive Dedication Regime. Deadlines and Procedures for Complaints and Appeals: Candidates may, if they so wish, comment on the draft decision to award the requested scholarship, at a hearing for interested parties within 10 business days, under the terms and for the purposes set forth in Article 121 of the Code of Administrative Procedure. Candidates have the right to complain to the evaluation panel within 10 business days regarding the commission or omission of any act. An appeal may be filed against the final decision of the application evaluation panel to the Rector within 10 business days of notification. Scholarship Contract : After receiving all required documentation, a scholarship contract will be signed with the selected candidate(s) in accordance with the attached template. Evaluation of Fellow( s): At the end of each fellowship contract period, the advisor will evaluate the fellow(s)' work by applying the following criteria, in accordance with the attached template: a) Achievement of objectives (80%) – Assessment of the extent to which the objectives and tasks outlined in the work plan have been achieved, taking into account the scientific and technical quality of the activities carried out, the rigour in the execution of procedures, and the results obtained. b) Behavioural competencies (10%) – Assessment of the competencies demonstrated during the period under review, particularly organisational skills, autonomy, responsibility, scientific rigour, and the ability to integrate into and collaborate with the research team. c) Personal attitude (10%) – Assessment of the commitment, interest, motivation, and availability demonstrated in carrying out research activities, as well as initiative and receptiveness to the guidance and recommendations provided by the supervisory team. The University of Algarve reserves the right to cancel the fellowship award process, within the scope of the Project in question, whenever funding is not awarded or the scholarship duration exceeds the project completion date. description: The Max-Born Institute invites applications for a PhD student (f/m/d) for the joint German-French project “FEMTO-switch” on ultrafast dynamics of photoswitches funded jointly by DFG and ANR. The main objective of FEMTO-switch is to establish rational grounds as to how the chemical structure of ultrafast photo-switches controls the molecular energetics and excited state dynamics of ultrafast photo-switches at the conical intersections. To this end, we will employ femtosecond UV/VIS/NIR and photoelectron spectroscopy (fs-PES) in the liquid phase, coupled to quantum chemistry calculations. The advertised position is for the experimental research using femtosecond photoelectron spectoscopy in liquids. Project objectives: Development of time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (TRPES) in the liquid phase with UV pump and XUV probe in application to samples of biomimetic chromophores at low concentrations. Investigation of oxindole-based and oxopyrrole based chromophores. Expected results: Improved sensitivity and stability of TRPES for different solvents and solutes of low solubility. Experimental protocols for biomimetic samples. Experimental and theoretical investigation of oxindole switches (in collaboration with project partners). Dynamics of novel biomimetic switches developed in FEMTO-switch. Techniques to be used: Time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy in liquid phase using femtosecond XUV pulses Requirements: We are seeking highly motivated, talented, and excellent candidates for this position. Applicants must hold a Master’s or Diploma degree in chemistry or physics, with good knowledge in femtosecond molecular dynamics and ultrafast laser physics. Prior experience in ultrafast spectroscopy would be an advantage. Very good verbal and written communications skills in English are required. Our offer: The position is available immediately for 3 years. The payment will be according to the German TVöD salary scheme for scientists in public research institutions (part-time 75% for PhD students). The MBI promotes an equity-based workplace and places particular emphasis on fostering career opportunities for women. Qualified women are therefore strongly encouraged to apply. If equally qualified, applicants with a disability will be given preference (Schwerbehinderung nach Sozialgesetzbuch IX). The MBI supports the reconcilability of family and working life and is certified by the audit workandfamily (audit berufundfamilie) as family-friendly. MBI is committed to a diverse, prejudice-aware working environment. The MBI follows the “Charta of Diversity” (Charta der Vielfalt) and implements the Diversity and Inclusion strategy as set up by the Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V.. Please upload your application, including cover letter (specifying why you are interested in the position), curriculum vitae, certificates and description of previous professional activities electronically via the MBI online recruiting platform at https://mbi-berlin.de/career . Official supervision will be given by Dr. Oleg Kornilov at MBI with affiliation to the physics department of Freie Universität Berlin. The advertisement is open with immediate effect and will remain open until November 8, 2026. For further information about the project, please contact Oleg Kornilov ( kornilov@mbi-berlin.de ).

Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Welcome to Maastricht University! How can we make osteoarthritis care more accessible, integrated and sustainable? And how can we bring the right care closer to people’s everyday lives? As a Junior Researcher, you will contribute to the European EUcare4OA project and help develop, implement and evaluate new approaches to osteoarthritis care across Europe. Junior Researcher Integrated Care and Osteoarthritis Our goal: The EUcare4OA (Community-Driven, Accessible, and Resilient Ecosystem for Osteoarthritis Care) project is a European research initiative focused on transforming osteoarthritis (OA) care across Europe. Partners from the Netherlands, Belgium and Sweden work together to develop, implement and evaluate an integrated, community-based care model. The aim is to help people with osteoarthritis receive the right care, at the right place, at the right time. EUcare4OA builds on the successful Beweeghuis Maastricht-Heuvelland model. The project aims to strengthen primary and community care by bringing together physiotherapy, patient self-management, community-based support and digital health solutions in one scalable care pathway. As a Junior Researcher, you will contribute to several work packages within the project and help translate research into practice. Your colleagues: You will be employed by CAPHRI (Care and Public Health Research Institute) at Maastricht University, while carrying out your work at Beweeghuis Maastricht-Heuvelland, embedded within the Department of Orthopedic Surgery at Maastricht University Medical Center+ (MUMC+). The Care and Public Health Research Institute (CAPHRI) www.caphri.nl aims to contribute to a healthy society for all through high-quality, methodologically innovative, interdisciplinary and socially relevant research. CAPHRI conducts research to understand and improve health, care and well-being, with a particular focus on prevention, participation, societal relevance, efficiency, and the value of care. You will be part of a multidisciplinary team. Your colleagues include orthopedic surgeons, physiotherapists, researchers, general practitioners, exercise coaches, policymakers and patient representatives. You will also collaborate closely with international project partners from the Netherlands, Belgium and Sweden. Together, we are developing stepped-care pathways that aim to improve the accessibility, quality and sustainability of osteoarthritis care. What you do As a Junior Researcher, you will contribute to research activities across several EUcare4OA work packages. Your work will combine research, collaboration and the practical implementation and evaluation of integrated care . Your activities include: Supporting comparative analyses of osteoarthritis care models in the participating countries. Collecting, managing and analysing quantitative and qualitative research data. Conducting literature reviews and contributing to evidence synthesis. Supporting stakeholder interviews, focus groups and co-creation workshops with patients, healthcare professionals, policymakers and community partners. Supporting the development and evaluation of integrated osteoarthritis care pathways. Assisting with pilot implementation and data collection within regional care networks. Contributing to project reports, scientific publications, presentations and dissemination activities. Collaborating with international project partners from the Netherlands, Belgium and Sweden. Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we’d love to meet you. What you bring We’re not looking for checkboxes; we’re interested in who you are and what you bring. Do you recognize yourself in this? You: Have a Master’s degree and/or a PHD in Health Sciences, Human Movement Sciences, Public Health, Epidemiology, Physiotherapy, Biomedical Sciences, Healthcare Policy or a related field. Have an affinity with healthcare research and innovation , and an interest in integrated care, implementation science and community-based healthcare. Have research skills, including experience with literature reviews, evidence synthesis and quantitative and/or qualitative research methods. Experience with data analysis software is an asset. Have strong analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills and are able to manage multiple tasks while working independently. Have excellent communication in Dutch (C1 level) and English. You enjoy working with researchers, healthcare professionals, patients and international project partners in a multidisciplinary environment . What we offer At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer: A 12-month contract (0,8 fte) with the prospect of a permanent contract based on mutual satisfaction. A gross monthly salary between €3706,00 and €5760,00 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus. 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours. Flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home. Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas. A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with. A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities. An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe. This one-year appointment offers an opportunity to contribute to meaningful research and further develop your research skills. Depending on your performance, motivation and the availability of funding, there may be an opportunity to continue the research as part of a PhD trajectory. About the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML) FHML is committed to health in the broadest sense: from molecule to human, and from healthcare to prevention. We train healthcare professionals and researchers through innovative educational programmes and conduct groundbreaking research in health and well-being. As part of Maastricht UMC+ (MUMC+), our international and interdisciplinary community forms a unique collaboration between university and academic hospital, where education, research, and care come together. Interested? Want to know more about this position or what it’s like to work at our university? Reach out to dr. Thomay Hoelen at thomay.hoelen@mumc.nl . The end date of the publication is November 8, 2026. Apply now via the button below. We look forward to getting to know you! About Maastricht University At Maastricht University, we collaboratively seek solutions to help move the world forward. We do this with 23,300 students and 5,400 employees across 5 regional locations, 6 faculties, and more than 70 research institutes. We encourage you to push boundaries and discover new opportunities for yourself and the world around you. Together, we can find the answers for tomorrow. The vacancy is open for internal and external candidates. In case of equal qualifications, internal candidates will be prioritized. At Maastricht University, we prefer to contact potential candidates directly. We therefore kindly ask that no agencies or intermediaries submit offers or approaches. Maastricht University is committed to promoting and nurturing a diverse and inclusive community. We believe that diversity in our staff and student population contributes to the quality of research and education at UM, and strive to enable this through inclusive policies and innovative projects led by teams of staff and students. We encourage you to apply for this position. No Offer Description We are looking for a talented and motivated Research AI Engineer to join the Artificial Intelligence in Medicine Lab (BCN-AIM, www.bcn-aim.org ) at the University of Barcelona, as part of TrustAI-ES ( https://bcn-aim.org/our_projects/trustai-es/ ), an innovative Spanish national research project funded by the Spanish Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities (MICIU/AEI) and co-funded by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF). The successful candidate will contribute to the development, implementation and validation of artificial intelligence models for heart failure, with a particular focus on federated learning, Generative AI for medical image and video synthesis, and trustworthy and fair AI. The candidate will work under the direct supervision of Dr. Polyxeni Gkontra, Principal Investigator of TrustAI-ES, Assistant Professor at the University of Barcelona and Senior Researcher at BCN-AIM. The position will also offer opportunities to collaborate on other European-funded research projects within the lab, depending on the candidate's interests, and with international academic and clinical partners. What will you do? Contribute to the full AI development lifecycle, from data preprocessing and integration to model development, implementation, deployment and validation. Develop, implement and validate machine learning and deep learning models for cardiovascular applications, particularly heart failure. Contribute to the development of fair federated learning aggregation techniques and their implementation and deployment across participating hospitals. Work on state-of-the-art Generative AI approaches for medical image and video synthesis and their application to cardiovascular AI. Implement trustworthy and fair AI approaches to improve the reliability, robustness and equity of AI models. Collaborate with an interdisciplinary team of AI researchers, engineers and clinical experts. Essential qualifications: A university degree (Bachelor's, Master's or equivalent) in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Artificial Intelligence or a related discipline. Proficiency in Python Knowledge and experience in Machine Learning and/or Deep Learning. Desirable qualifications and experience: A Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Artificial Intelligence or a related discipline will be highly valued. Knowledge and experience in Federated Learning and/or Generative AI Experience in medical image analysis and/or artificial intelligence applications in healthcare. We are looking for someone with strong technical skills, enthusiasm for research and medical applications of AI, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an international research environment. We offer: The opportunity to join a dynamic research group working at the forefront of AI for healthcare. Research experience within a prestigious university (1st position in Spain). Hands-on experience in cutting-edge research on federated learning, Generative AI for medical image/video synthesis and trustworthy AI. An international and multidisciplinary research environment, with opportunities to collaborate with academic and clinical partners. Flexible working arrangements, including the possibility of teleworking. The opportunity to live and work in Barcelona, one of Europe's most vibrant and attractive cities. About the project TrustAI-ES: Trustworthy AI for Heart Failure Risk Assessment in Spain through Federated Learning and Image Synthesis TrustAI-ES aims to develop innovative and trustworthy AI solutions for heart failure risk assessment by leveraging federated learning and medical image/video synthesis. The project focuses on developing privacy-preserving and fair AI models that can learn from data distributed across different hospitals, without requiring the centralisation of sensitive patient information. At the same time, generative AI for medical image/video synthesis will be used to expand the available training data, particularly for under-represented groups in Spain. This is essential for ensuring algorithmic fairness and reducing bias in AI models. The successful candidate will contribute to the implementation and validation of these approaches, helping advance reliable and equitable AI solutions for cardiovascular medicine. About BCN-AIM The successful candidate will join the Artificial Intelligence in Medicine Lab (BCN-AIM, www.bcn-aim.org ), based at the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science of the University of Barcelona. Our team brings together more than 30 enthusiastic academics, researchers, students and research managers, with expertise in data science, machine and deep learning, biomedical informatics, trustworthy AI, and health-related applications. The research group has an established track record in coordinating and participating in European and international projects (18 projects, more than 12 million Euros over the last 5 years) in biomedical data science and medical AI (e.g. EuCanImage, euCanSHare, EarlyCause, LongITools, HealthyCloud, RadioVal, DataTools4Heart, Youth-GEMs, HappyMums, AIMIX, AI4HF, YOUTHreach, DVPS, AIXPERT, AFRICAI-RI, AIFIX, STAGE). About the institution The University of Barcelona (UB), founded in 1450, is one of the oldest universities in Spain. It comprises a student body of 84,370 and 4,548 research staff members. With 73 undergraduate programs, 273 graduate programs and 48 doctorate programs, UB is the largest university in Barcelona and Catalonia. The UB is ranked the first Spanish university according to several rankings (QS World University Rankings 2022, Shanghai Ranking 2022). It is particularly interested in fostering international relations and, for many years, has managed an average of 150 European projects per year. The University of Barcelona is part of the prestigious League of European Universities Research (LERU). Gross salary per year: 39.863,56 € (Senior Technician, Group I). No Offer Description We are looking for a motivated researcher who combines strong quantitative skills with an interest in critical materials, supply chains, and sustainability. What are you going to do? You will investigate supply chains across material extraction, processing, manufacturing, use, and recycling. The research will examine how disruptions propagate between countries, sectors, and stages of production, and how different responses influence supply security, economic performance, and environmental outcomes. Potential research directions include mapping dependencies and bottlenecks in critical material and clean energy supply chains; modelling the effects of trade restrictions, production interruptions, and changing demand; and evaluating strategies such as supplier diversification, recycling, material substitution, and technological innovation. The specific research focus will be developed with Dr Sun, taking account of your expertise and the project objectives. Depending on the research questions, methods may include network analysis, material flow analysis, input–output modelling, optimisation, and scenario-based simulation. Your main responsibilities will be to: Develop and apply quantitative models to assess supply chain vulnerabilities, disruption impacts, and recovery pathways. Compile, integrate, and critically evaluate data on material flows, international trade, production capacities, and clean energy technologies. Compare resilience strategies and assess their implications for resource use and environmental sustainability. Prepare research articles for peer-reviewed journals and communicate findings at scientific meetings. Collaborate with colleagues and contribute to the research activities of the group. Maintain transparent, well-documented datasets and reproducible analytical workflows. About the position The University of Groningen invites applications for a one-year postdoctoral position in supply chain resilience, working with Dr Xin Sun. The position focuses on understanding how supply chains can withstand disruptions, recover from shocks, and adapt to changing geopolitical, economic, and environmental conditions, with particular attention to critical materials and clean energy technologies. The transition to a low-carbon economy depends on reliable supplies of materials and technologies. Concentrated production, international trade dependencies, and disruptions across interconnected supply chains can create vulnerabilities that affect the pace and sustainability of this transition. This project will develop quantitative approaches to identify these vulnerabilities, assess the consequences of disruptions, and evaluate strategies that strengthen resilience while supporting sustainability goals. Experience in quantitative modelling and data analysis, with proficiency in Python, R, MATLAB, Julia, or a comparable programming language. Expertise in at least one relevant method, such as network analysis, material flow analysis, input–output analysis, optimisation, or systems modelling. The ability to formulate research questions, critically assess data and assumptions, and conduct independent research. Evidence of strong scientific writing, demonstrated through publications, manuscripts, or doctoral research. Excellent written and spoken English and the ability to collaborate in an international research environment. Experience with critical material supply chains, clean energy technologies, international trade data, disruption modelling, or life cycle assessment would be an advantage. Applicants with strong transferable methodological expertise are also encouraged to apply. description: 272 Application Deadline: November 11, 2026 Applications are now open for the 2027 Gates Foundation AI Fellows Program. The AI Fellows Program at the Gates Foundation is dedicated to accelerating the responsible and impactful use of AI in global health, development, and education. You will be joining the first Africa-based AI Fellows cohort where you work alongside our Africa team, our partners and government counterparts to bring AI tooling to clarify and make decisions that matter most. Each fellow will be assigned 1–2 high-priority projects that will help accelerate achieving the foundation’s mission. Note: This is a 12-month limited term employment position based in Abuja, Nigeria / Addis Ababa, Ethiopia / Johannesburg, South Africa / Nairobi, Kenya. Candidates must be able to legally work in the country where this position is located without visa sponsorship and relocation support will not be provided. Sample project areas include: Build decision-support tools across multiple African countries that unify disparate financing flow systems, conducts a periodic bottleneck diagnostics and supports informed decision-making. Design and prototype a solution to reduce stockouts of essential medicines at district and facility level, targeting countries facing drawdown of US Government-funded logistics management capacity. Strengthen health planning and supply chain systems by building an AI decision-support tool that ranks interventions against budget ceilings and traces prioritized interventions through procurement and cash release, developing a predictive analytics layer to forecast stock-out risk and flag redistribution opportunities before expiry Your Role The AI Fellows Program at the Gates Foundation is designed to accelerate the responsible and impactful use of AI in global health, development, and education. Our goal is to attract top-tier, mission-aligned AI talent to drive innovation in these areas. Building on the success of our US and India-based cohorts, we are expanding our program to Africa. As a Gates AI Fellow, you will join a prestigious cohort applying AI for public good and gain career-defining experience, access to Gates’ powerful network, and exposure to senior leadership. This role offers the unique opportunity to collaborate across multiple divisions within the Foundation—including Global Health (GH), Gender Equality (GE), Global Development (GD), and Global Growth & Opportunity (GGO)— to bridge the possibilities of frontier AI technology with the realities of deployment to create real, meaningful impact. Over the course of 12 months, each AI Fellow will be assigned to high-priority projects , embedded within our Africa team. Fellows may contribute to multiple AI-oriented projects over the course of the fellowship, including concurrently, and should be comfortable adapting their technical approach as project needs evolve. Requirements Education : Candidates must hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree (in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Applied Math or relevant field). Experience: At least 2 years of experience applying AI solutions, preferably in health or agricultural systems. AI Technology : Strong foundation in modern AI/ML, including ML/AI modeling, model evaluation, and hands-on experience with LLMs, combined with software engineering and data skills needed to build end-to-end applied solutions. Evidence may come from applied coursework, research, internships, or early professional experience. AI Applications: Demonstrated interest in applying AI to fields such as health systems, public financial management, supply chain and logistics, with enthusiasm and literacy to use modern AI tools safely and pragmatically (direct AI research experience not required). Candidates should be comfortable learning across adjacent technical areas – such as data engineering, time-series analysis, optimization, information retrieval, or decision-support systems – as project needs evolve. Collaborative Mindset: Strong teamwork and adaptability, with experience working cross-functionally in complex environments. Communication Skills: Demonstrated ability to clearly articulate technical concepts and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences. Mission-Driven Ethos: Deep motivation to apply AI responsibly for public good, with alignment to equitable development and global health impact. Builder and Teacher Approach : Hands-on experience building prototypes with LLMs and other modern AI tools (e.g., using open-source tools or API-based platforms), with the judgment to connect AI components to the broader data and software systems needed for real-world use. Willingness to share findings openly and ability to teach and enable others, not just deliver technical outputs. Benefits Apply AI where it matters most : Work on problems core to the Foundation’s mission—health, development, and education so more people can live healthy, productive lives. Drive outsized results in LMICs : Aim solutions at countries and communities the Foundation prioritize, where innovation can move the needle fastest. Advance digital public goods: Contribute to safe, inclusive digital public infrastructure and health innovation efforts where AI can accelerate access and equity. Partner with Program Strategy Teams to deliver tangible prototypes, tools, and analyses. Tap into a uniquely powerful network: Collaborate across multilaterals, NGOs, academia, and industry through the Foundation’s partnership model. Stand on a global platform : Benefit from the credibility and reach of a foundation funding work in over 140 countries. Lead from day one: Own high-priority projects with clear outcomes and partners. Grow faster with expert mentorship: Learn from leaders across AI, health, development, and policy while building a portfolio of real-world impact. For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the Gates Foundation AI Fellows Program
