No Offer Description The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for the post of Associate Professor (Tenure Track) of AI technologies and industrial applications at the Department of Technical Physics of the Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology on the Kuopio campus. The position will be filled from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application no later than 11 November 2026. Role and salary At the Department of Technical Physics (website) , research and education are organized around four main focus areas: medical physics and engineering, aerosol physics, computational science and engineering, and materials engineering). The department hosts several research groups and is involved in research conducted in two Research Council of Finland’s Centre of Excellence Programmes and three Research Council of Finland’s Flagship Programmes. The degree programme in Technical Physics was launched in autumn 2023, and the department will launch a new Degree Programme in Pharmaceutical Engineering together with the School of Pharmacy in 2027. The Department of Technical Physics is ambitious and growing unit. The research and teaching field of the Associate Professor is AI technologies and industrial applications. The person to be appointed to the post is required to have expertise and demonstrated achievements in, e.g., AI solutions related to the planning of industrial equipment, processes and services and user-oriented applications, and in their optimisation. The key research and teaching themes of the role will also be developed by utilising the views and needs of companies operating in the region. The duties of the Associate Professor include the acquisition of external research funding, the launching and management of research projects, high-quality publishing activities, and teaching and supervision duties related to the field. The Associate Professor will also be responsible for international research cooperation and networking in the field of research. The post also includes societal expert and interaction activities. The post of Associate Professor will be filled for a four-year term as of 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). The post is filled for a fixed term due to it being a Tenure Track position. A probationary period is applied to all new members of the UEF staff. The criteria, objectives and results to be achieved during the term, which are required for progression to the next level of the tenure track (Professor), shall be agreed in detail with the person appointed as Associate Professor at the time of signing the employment contract. Fulfilment of the agreed criteria is a prerequisite for promotion to the permanent professorship through the tenure track. External expert evaluation will be used in this recruitment. Expert statements are part of the overall evaluation process for the position. Interviews related to the filling of the position will be arranged separately. The salary of the post is based on the salary system of Finnish universities. The salary is based on level 7 (EUR 4,525 /month) of the job requirement level chart of the salary system for the teaching and research staff of Finnish universities. In addition to the job-related salary element, the salary is supplemented with a personal salary element, which can be a maximum of 50% of the job-related salary element. At the beginning of the employment, the total salary will be approximately EUR 5,255 – 5,520 / month. Our requirements and expectations We require you to hold a suitable doctoral degree have good teaching skills have good skills in spoken and written English. The language of instruction in the position may be English demonstrated research expertise in the research area of the position. Fulfil the qualification requirements of a Professor by the end of the Tenure Track term. The evaluation will be launched no later than six months before the end of the term, unless otherwise has been agreed upon with the party concerned. Teaching skills are evaluated based on the documents submitted by the applicant. The evaluation of teaching skills focuses on your teaching and supervision experience, as well as on your views related to the planning and implementation of teaching, as presented in your teaching portfolio (see the required attachments of the application). The following will be considered an advantage experience in industry collaboration a track record in industrial AI research and/or applications a proven track record of successfully securing research and project funding experience in conducting industry-driven research in the field. Your benefits You will have access to the university’s staff benefits, including the opportunity for flexible multi-location work excellent opportunities for professional development and continuous learning extensive occupational health care a broad selection of staff training staff discount on lunch in our campus restaurants, as well as on a range of other services affordable sports services Please read more in the Work at UEF section on our website . You will have an opportunity to work in an interesting, meaningful and diverse role as part of our international, creative, participatory and inclusive academic community. Enjoy your life in Finland! Known for its cleanliness, welfare know-how, modern technology and superb education system, Finland is an exotic and safe country to work in. Please visit the Life in Finland section on our website to learn more. How to apply? Submit your application by using our electronic application form no later than 11 November 2026 by 23:59 (midnight) Finnish time (UTC+2). The following documents must be enclosed with the application: CV ( Template for CV, TENK web page ) a portfolio of teaching merits (Instructions, a portfolio of teaching merits PDF ) a list of publications ( Instructions, Research Council of Finland Web page ) a separate list of the publications (10, numbered and indexed) and other works with which the applicant wishes to demonstrate their qualification and merits for the post the publications and other works referred to in the above list with which the applicant wishes to demonstrate their qualification and merits for the post a short, written description (2–4 pages) of the merits and activities relevant to the post, including the applicant’s views on how to develop research and teaching in the field copies of academic degree certificates / diplomas (highest degree). The application with appendices should be submitted in English (excluding any publications published in Finnish) in case the applicants’ qualification and merits are assessed by international experts. The applicant must ensure that the contact details specified in the application remain up-to-date throughout the recruitment process. If your degree certificate is not in English, Finnish, or Swedish, you must provide official English translations of your degree certificate documents. All translations must be issued by the awarding educational institution or an authorized translator. Each page of the official translation must bear the translator's stamp and/or signature. Official translations must be accurate translations of the original documents. Translations made by the applicants themselves will not be accepted. Questions? description: PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development Referenzcode: 1057 Arbeitsort: Geesthacht Bewerbungsfrist: 12.11.2026 The Institute of Material and Process Design at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon is offering a 4-year PhD position in the field of computational materials engineering, machine learning, and digital twins for advanced lightweight materials. The focus of the PhD project will be the development of a physics-guided digital twin framework for magnesium alloys by integrating experimental characterization, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, precipitation modeling, and machine learning approaches to establish quantitative composition-process-structure-property relationships. Building upon recently developed machine-learning approaches for structure-property prediction in extruded magnesium alloys, the project aims to advance toward a next-generation Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework capable of predicting microstructure evolution and resulting mechanical properties across previously unseen processing conditions and material states. The candidate will work closely with interdisciplinary teams combining expertise in magnesium alloy development, thermomechanical processing, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, machine learning, and advanced experimental characterization. The objective of the project is to bridge the gap between purely data-driven materials modeling and mechanistic microstructure simulations by combining crystal plasticity, dynamic recrystallization, precipitation kinetics, and machine learning into a unified digital-twin framework. The resulting methodologies shall enable accelerated alloy and process design by leveraging experimentally validated physics-guided surrogate models with improved extrapolation capabilities beyond the limits of conventional machine-learning approaches. This work directly contributes to the digital transformation of materials development and manufacturing technologies for future lightweight engineering applications. Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. Your tasks - development of physics-guided machine-learning models for composition-process-structure-property relationships in magnesium alloys - combination of crystal plasticity, phase-field, precipitation, and machine-learning approaches into a unified digital twin framework - implementation of simulation and machine-learning workflows in Python (e.g. PyTorch, Scikit-Learn, etc.) - incorporation of experimental microstructure and texture characterization data obtained from optical microscopy, SEM, EBSD, XRD, and mechanical testing - investigation of uncertainty quantification and explainable artificial intelligence methods (XAI) for materials modeling - validation of computational predictions in collaboration with experimental and modeling researchers - publication and presentation of scientific results in leading international journals, conferences, and workshops - active contribution to the establishment of next-generation ICME and digital-twin methodologies for sustainable lightweight materials design Your profile -master?s degree in mechanical engineering, materials science, computational engineering, physics, applied mathematics, data science, or a related discipline -strong interest in computational materials science, digital twins, and machine learning -good programming skills in Python -experience with machine-learning methods and common scientific Python libraries is desirable -knowledge of computational mechanics, finite element methods, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, or thermodynamic simulations is advantageous -experience in analysis of experimental materials-science data is beneficial -ability to work independently as well as within an interdisciplinary research team -strong analytical and problem-solving skills -highly proficient in spoken and written English motivation to conduct high-quality research at the interface of materials science, mechanical engineering, and artificial intelligence Our offer -an exciting and varied job in a research centre with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations -an International Welcome Office with guest accommodation -6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's Day - social benefits under the collective agreement for the German public sector and remuneration up to pay grade 13 (EntgO Bund) - very good work-life balance; options for mobile and flexible working - a well-connected research campus, good networking opportunities, a subsidized Deutschlandticket (job ticket) subject to certain conditions, and charging facilities for electric vehicles - individual opportunities for training and development - an excellent technical infrastructure and modern workplace equipment - PhD Buddy Program - a family-friendly working environment with childcare options, e.g. a daycare center close to the workplace - workplace health promotion programmes, e.g. an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) -corporate benefits - a varied offer in the canteen on campus Severely disabled persons and those equaling severely disabled persons who are equally suitable for the position will be considered preferentially within the framework of legal requirements. Interested? Then we are looking forward to receiving your comprehensive application documents (cover letter, CV, transcripts, certificates, etc.) until November 12th, 2026. description: 25 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Karolinska Institutet, doctoral positions Research Field Biological sciences » Biology Medical sciences » Medicine Medical sciences » Other Chemistry » Molecular chemistry Chemistry » Biochemistry Chemistry » Analytical chemistry Biological sciences » Biological engineering Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 13 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Sweden Type of Contract Other Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required. The research group The project is based within the research team of Maarten van de Klundert, which is part of senior professor Anders Sönnerborgs activities at the department of Medicine, Huddinge, Centrum of Infectious Medicine – Clinical Infectious Disease. The team has a strong research focus on HIV-1. The PhD position is based at ANA Futura Laboratory, Campus Flemingsberg, a modern and international research environment with access to advanced infrastructure and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration. The position will be closely integrated with the clinical microbiology laboratory at Karolinska University Laboratory, the National Reference Laboratory for HIV-1 and Retroviruses. You will work in a collaborative environment involving researchers with complementary expertise in molecular virology, HIV-1 immunology, and bioinformatics. The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student The PhD position is part of the national Graduate School: Biomedical Laboratory Scientists for Excellence – Future Educators in Health and Medical Care, (BioLabX). Therefore, only graduated Biomedical laboratory scientists are eligible to apply for the position In this doctoral project, you will investigate the HIV-1 reservoir in clinical samples from people living with HIV-1. It is closely connected to an ongoing clinical cohort at Department of Infectious Diseases, Karolinska University Hospital, and combines established clinical sampling with molecular and bioinformatic analyses of HIV-1 proviruses. You will establish and optimise workflows for the analysis of HIV-1 proviral DNA to characterise HIV-1 proviral sequences with respect to genetic diversity, viral subtype, drug-resistance mutations, hypermutation, and other sequence features. For data analysis, you will use advanced bioinformatics and phylogenetic analysis. You will also be involved in biobanking of all incoming samples, and later characterise immunological characteristics of selected study participants, for instance by FACS analysis, ELIspot assays, assessing HIV reactivation and more. In addition to mandatory courses specific to the PhD education at Karolinska Institutet, the BioLabX program includes a shared course package consisting of two subject-specific doctoral courses. The program also comprises a seminar series, workshops, and annual retreats that are mandatory for the doctoral students. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment full of expertise and curiosity. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. As a doctoral student you are offered an individual research project, a well-educated supervisor, a vast range of elective courses and the opportunity to work in a leading research group. Karolinska Institutet collaborates with prominent universities from all around the world, which ensures opportunities for international exchanges. You will be employed on a doctoral studentship which means that you receive a contractual salary. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care. Eligibility requirements for doctoral education In order to participate in the selection for a doctoral position, you must meet the following general (A) and specific (B) eligibility requirements at latest by the application deadline. No Offer Description How do individuals and civil society organisations take platforms and data-driven companies to court? And what can litigation under the Digital Services Act (DSA) learn from collective data protection actions under the GDPR? We are looking for a student assistant to help us investigate. Join us! How do individuals and civil society organisations take platforms and data-driven companies to court? And what can litigation under the Digital Services Act (DSA) learn from collective data protection actions under the GDPR? We are looking for a student assistant to help us investigate. This project, funded through UvA DDT seed funding, connects two ongoing research projects at the Amsterdam Law School. The first maps the private enforcement of the DSA before national courts, including a DSA case tracker published through the DSA Observatory. The second, APPLIED , examines the collective private enforcement of the GDPR through a systematic analysis of case law across Europe. Together, we compare why and how (collective) private enforcement is pursued in both fields: who brings claims, on what legal basis, and with what remedies and results. The project is a collaboration between the Department of Private Law (Amsterdam Centre for Transformative Private Law, ACT) and the Institute for Information Law (IViR). What you will do Identify, log and code new DSA private enforcement cases for the DSA case tracker (to be launched shortly), keeping it up to date as a public resource Write and review case summaries for the tracker, based on judgments, filings and other primary sources Update the APPLIED case law analysis of collective GDPR actions with recent developments, including new national case law, representative actions and CJEU judgments Support the comparison between the two fields, which feeds into a co-authored academic article and a DSA Observatory blog post Help maintain a shared literature library and assist with organising an online expert workshop with litigators and academics Your profile You are a Master's student in Law, for instance in Information Law or Private Law; students from other programmes with a solid legal background are also welcome to apply You have a strong interest in platform regulation, data protection, collective redress and access to justice You work precisely and systematically, write clearly and concisely, and are comfortable with spreadsheets or databases You have excellent English and can read legal texts in at least one other EU language; German, Dutch or French are especially valuable You are available for the full contract period and can work flexibly in consultation with the team What we offer Hands-on experience in comparative and empirical legal research at the intersection of private law and information law A place in a small, collaborative team spanning ACT, IViR and the DSA Observatory, with room for your own initiative Co-authorship of a DSA Observatory blog post presenting the project's findings A temporary contract of 10 hours per week from 1 November 2026 to 30 June 2027. Your salary is € 3.230,00 to € 3.288,00 gross per month on a full-time basis (38 hours per week; salary scale SA, depending on your year of study), plus 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% year-end bonus. The Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities applies. You will work in this team The University of Amsterdam is the largest university in the Netherlands, with the broadest spectrum of degree programmes. With over 5,000 students and more than 500 staff members, the Amsterdam Law School is one of the larger law faculties in the Netherlands. We educate lawyers who know how to apply the law effectively with the aim of making a real contribution to solving social problems. The Amsterdam Law School stands for progressive and trail-blazing education and research, for stronger legal institutions, solutions to social problems and a better and juster society. Please apply through the red button, uploading your CV, a short motivation letter (max. one page) and a recent grade list. The deadline for applications is 13 November 2026. The research agenda of the CyI is pursued at its five Research Centres, namely: The Computation-based Science and Technology Research Centre (CaSToRC) The Science and Technology in Archaeology and Culture Research Centre (STARC) The Energy Environment Water Research Centre (EEWRC) The Climate and Atmosphere Research Centre (CARE-C) The Science and Technology Driven Policy and Innovation Research Centre (STeDI-RC) Considerable cross-centre interaction is a characteristic of the Institute’s scientific ethos. The Cyprus Institute invites applications for a highly qualified and motivated Researcher to join the Institute’s STARC Centre on a full-time basis (100% FTE) for its premises at Athalassas Campus. The successful candidate will be involved in advancing digital approaches to the documentations, management, analysis and simulation of the historic built environment through Heritage Building Information Modelling (HBIM), parametric modelling, reality-based documentation, information management and interoperable digital workflows. The position focuses on developing and implementing innovative methodologies for digital heritage documentation, semantic enrichment of heritage information, standards-based interoperability, and the development of digital twins with applications in conservation, building performance assessment, and sustainable heritage management. Particular emphasis will be given on BIM-based information management, open data standards, interoperability on digital platforms, and the development of scalable methodologies for managing complex heritage datasets. The role will also support the translation of research outcomes into practical applications for heritage conservation, decision-making, and sustainable management of the built environment. The successful candidate is expected to demonstrate a strong academic and research background, proven expertise in digital heritage technologies, BIM-based methodologies, and interdisciplinary research, together with excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaborative skills. description: Every year, GEAS opens its programme to a new group of doctoral candidates. GEAS offers a structured three-year doctoral programme embedded within a four-year PhD process, with a regional focus on East Asia (China, Japan, Korea). Doctoral dissertations analyse modern or contemporary East Asia in the fields of politics, society, economy, culture, law or history. Doctoral candidates are admitted for the fall semester, starting 1 October 2027. Successful applicants hold an above-average master’s degree in either area studies (Chinese, Japanese or Korean Studies) or a discipline represented at the Graduate School with a focus on East Asia — Political Science, International Law, Public Law, History, Cultural Studies, Social and Cultural Anthropology, Business and Economics, Performance Studies or Transregional Studies. Applicants are not expected to contact potential supervisors before applying, but are encouraged to review the profiles of GEAS members to check that their project fits a supervisor’s research profile. For full details, see Requirements . The language of communication is English (C1). Successful candidates also have skills in Chinese, Japanese or Korean at B2 or higher. Applicants with native skills in English or one of the East Asian languages have another modern foreign language at B2 or higher. Please note: dissertation topics in Linguistics, Literary Studies, Education, Film, Media and/or Communication Studies cannot be supervised. Applications for the 2027 intake are open from 15 September 2026 to 15 November 2026. Please register and apply online through the Dahlem Research School Application Portal .

description: The internationally oriented doctoral program History and Cultural Studies (HCS) invites applications for up to ten study places. The program is part of the Department of History and Cultural Studies and is a member of the Dahlem Research School. Target group: The Program offers graduate students with an excellent academic record a structured, research-oriented curriculum in cultural studies with disciplinary and interdisciplinary elements for doctoral studies in one of the research areas of the Department of History and Cultural Studies. The PhD Program is a three-year curriculum. Courses are taught in English and German. Profile: The disciplines represented in the HCS program work historically, dealing with material, visual and written cultures. They research antique cultures as well as the present, examining literatures, textual traditions, and languages in the Near and Middle East, different regions in East Asia, religions, and cults. The doctoral program brings these subjects together in the common interest of combining broad approaches of cultural studies with subject-specific knowledge and competence and of forming a practice of interdisciplinary work. HCS considers both the tradition of Kulturwissenschaften taught in Germany and the Anglo-American cultural studies approach to (socio-)political questions. The program gives doctoral students the opportunity to develop and regularly discuss their own research based on these discursive traditions. Participation in the HCS requires both well-founded subject knowledge and a profound interest in theoretical and methodological issues on an interdisciplinary level.

SYNAPSE develops networks that adapt scheduling, routing and resource allocation to network conditions and clinical urgency. It also develops distributed and federated learning methods that adapt to connectivity, available resources and clinical priorities. The methods are evaluated in remote patient monitoring and hospital-at-home scenarios. Research areas include reinforcement learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning, graph and hypergraph representation learning, temporal graph neural networks, and network-aware federated learning. description: 24 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) Research Field Engineering » Control engineering Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 15 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Permanent Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Horizon Europe Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Join TU Delft and the EU-funded OPERA consortium. Push the frontier of general-purpose AI for robotics and tackle the fundamental tension between long-horizon reasoning and real-time safety guarantees. Job description Robots that operate for long periods among people must plan beyond the next few seconds while staying safe. They need to predict how their surroundings and the people in them will evolve, know how reliable these predictions are, and adapt their plans when the predictions fail. In the EU-funded OPERA project, TU Delft contributes to General-Purpose AI for robotics by developing methods that combine fast, reactive behavior with more deliberate reasoning, planning, and decision-making. In this PhD position, you will develop planning and decision-making methods that let robots act safely and reliably over long time horizons when their knowledge of the environment and of the people around them is incomplete. The research sits at the intersection of model-based planning and control and learning-based models, and addresses the trade-off between safety, performance, and real-time computation. You will formulate the methods and analyze their guarantees and failure modes. This research is connected to OPERA's tasks on GPAI-powered planning and decision-making, on long-term reasoning in human-centered environments, and on adaptive human-robot and robot-environment interaction. Depending on your background, the work may draw on optimal control and model predictive control, motion planning, probabilistic modeling and estimation, or learning-based methods. The emphasis is on methods with a clear formulation and well-understood failure modes, validated in simulation and on real robots. You will work in the Cognitive Robotics Department at TU Delft under the supervision of Prof. Robert Babuška and Dr. Laura Ferranti, and you will be embedded in the Reliable Robot Control Lab ( https://r2clab.com/ ). You will collaborate with OPERA partners across Europe on simulation, perception, and the OPERA open-source toolbox. Job requirements The ideal candidate for this PhD position has a strong background in control, optimization, or motion planning and is motivated by the question of how robots can plan safely and reliably over long time horizons. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds who want to work at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. You have: An MSc degree in Systems and Control, Robotics, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. A strong interest in safe planning and decision-making for robots, at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. A passion for rigorous, theoretically grounded research, combined with an eagerness to validate ideas in simulation and on real robots. Strong analytical and mathematical skills, in particular in optimization, probability and statistics, and dynamical systems. Excellent communication skills and proficiency in English (written and verbal), as required for academic publication and international collaboration. You are particularly encouraged to apply if you have experience in one or more of the following areas: Hands-on experience implementing optimization-based planners or controllers (e.g., model predictive control with acados or CasADi) in C++ or Python. Safe or robust control and planning under uncertainty. Learned dynamics or prediction models, model-based reinforcement learning. Uncertainty quantification, probabilistic or Bayesian modeling, state estimation. Long-horizon or hierarchical planning, prediction of human or multi-agent behavior. Real-robot deployment with ROS or ROS 2. As part of OPERA, you will travel to meet and collaborate with the project’s European partners and attend regular consortium meetings. We particularly encourage applications from women and other underrepresented groups, as we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive research environment. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Mechanical Engineering From chip to ship. From machine to human being. From idea to solution. Driven by a deep-rooted desire to understand our environment and discover its underlying mechanisms, research and education at the ME faculty focusses on fundamental understanding, design, production including application and product improvement, materials, processes and (mechanical) systems. ME is a dynamic and innovative faculty with high-tech lab facilities and international reach. It’s a large faculty but also versatile, so we can often make unique connections by combining different disciplines. This is reflected in ME’s outstanding, state-of-the-art education, which trains students to become responsible and socially engaged engineers and scientists. We translate our knowledge and insights into solutions to societal issues, contributing to a sustainable society and to the development of prosperity and well-being. That is what unites us in pioneering research, inspiring education and (inter)national cooperation. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. Do you want to experience working at our faculty? These videos will introduce you to some of our researchers and their work. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3059 - €3881 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service , offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information For more information, please reach out to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska [ l.ferranti@tudelft.nl , r.babuska@tudelft.nl ] Please do not use LinkedIn and other channels for applications or inquiries. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 15 November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: A letter of motivation explaining why you are the right candidate for this project An updated cv Exam transcipts from your Bachelor and Master A copy of your MSc thesis, or draft MSc thesis (or a link to access it) You can address your application to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements . No Offer Description Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), microscopic colitis, gastrointestinal eosinophilic disorders, and other disorders of gut–brain interaction represent a significant proportion of the conditions encountered in gastroenterology practice. These conditions are chronic and recurrent, yet reliable diagnostic biomarkers remain scarce and clinical management remains suboptimal. Intestinal barrier dysfunction, low-grade mucosal inflammation, and immune activation are shared features of several of these disorders and may contribute to symptom onset, persistence, and severity. Our research group aims to elucidate the genetic, sex-related, immunological, metabolic, cellular, and molecular mechanisms linking environmental factors, particularly stress, to intestinal barrier dysfunction, mucosal inflammation, and immune activation. Our research focuses primarily on IBS and related gastrointestinal disorders, with the overarching goal of understanding the mechanisms underlying their pathophysiology and clinical manifestations. We pursue an integrated, multidisciplinary, and translational research strategy that combines experimental studies in animal models with investigations in human cohorts. By bridging mechanistic research and clinical practice, we aim to identify novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for improving the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of IBS and related disorders. Our work also incorporates preclinical and clinical studies to facilitate the translation of mechanistic discoveries into clinically relevant advances and improved patient care. We are seeking a recognised postdoctoral researcher with a completed PhD and a minimum of three years’ postdoctoral experience, who is ready to take the next step in their research career. The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to deliver high-quality, rigorous and impactful research with increasing scientific autonomy, while contributing to a collaborative and interdisciplinary environment. You will be expected to publish in top-tier international journals, secure competitive research funding as Principal Investigator (PI) or Co-Principal Investigator (Co-PI) and play an active role in advancing the scientific objectives of the team. In addition, you will contribute to mentoring and supervising students and early-stage researchers, while supporting innovation activities, including the identification of intellectual property and engagement in research valorisation and commercialisation processes. description: 24 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Maastricht University (UM) Research Field Medical sciences » Medicine Researcher Profile Recognised Researcher (R2) Application Deadline 15 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Welcome to Maastricht University! What if we could slow down vascular ageing by targeting the cells where the first signs of ageing occur? Join an ambitious, NWO VICI-funded research project at CARIM (Cardiovascular Research Institute Maastricht) investigating the role of mesenchymal cells and their metabolism in vascular ageing. By combining multi-omics approaches with functional and metabolic studies, you will help identify new therapeutic targets to delay vascular ageing and cardiovascular disease. Postdoctoral Researcher: Reset Aged Vascular Function Our goal: Demonstrate causality of identified targets to reset fibroblast function and/or metabolism to rescue vascular dysfunction in ageing, hypertension and/or atherosclerosis. Your colleagues: You will be embedded in the group of Prof. Sluimer, embedded in the Pathology department and CARIM, which studies the role immune and mesenchymal cells in vascular pathologies, such as atherosclerosis and vascular ageing ( http://www.pathologie.mumc.nl/medewerkers/sluimer ). CARIM is one of the eight research institutes of the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML) of Maastricht University (UM). It is embedded in the Maastricht University Medical Center+ (Maastricht UMC+). Located in the heart of Europe, UM holds the distinction of being the most internationally diverse university in the Netherlands with more than half of our students and academic staff coming from abroad. In total, UM represents 100 different nationalities. The project centres on ageing of the vasculature and is supported by an NWO VICI grant. Vascular ageing, for which there is no treatment, accelerates cardiovascular disease. Until now research and therapies have only focussed on the inner layers of the vasculature to delay vascular ageing. However, the first signs of ageing occur in the perivascular layer. This project aims to adapt the function of cells in the perivascular layer to delay vascular ageing by analysing human and murine cells and arteries and animal models to create a cross-species multi-omics RNA and metabolic atlas. You will investigate gene leads that change with ageing using functional and metabolism assays and gain/loss of function studies. We expect this study will yield new treatment options for vascular ageing and delay cardiovascular disease. What you do Design, plan and perform experiments with cells, and tissues related to expression detection, function and metabolism of fibroblasts Design, plan and perform experiments with small animal models to study vascular ageing, hypertension and/or atherosclerosis Communicate results and ideas to colleagues and at conferences Supervise BSc/MSc/PhD-students Contribute to teaching activities for BSc/MSc students Contribute to grant development Optional: Analyse single cell sequencing datasets (R (i.e. Seurat) or Python) Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we’d love to meet you. What you bring We’re not looking for checkboxes; we’re interested in who you are and what you bring. Do you recognize yourself in this? You are curious and eager to learn, adapt easily to new situations, and are open to feedback to continuously develop your skills and improve your work. Furthermore: You have a PhD in Biology, Health Sciences or Medicine. You have demonstrable research experience in cardiovascular research and one or more related topics, such as vascular ageing, atherosclerosis, and/or fibroblast metabolism. You have the ability to independently perform one or more of the following techniques: metabolism assays, small animal models and/or myography. Experience with flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry and/or bioinformatics (e.g. R or Python) is considered an advantage. You have the ability to independently design and perform cell culture experiments. You have excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and enjoy working in an international research environment. What we offer At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer: A 12-month contract (1 FTE) with the prospect of a 12 month extension. A gross monthly salary of € 3.706 - € 5.760 based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week in scale 10.5). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus. 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours. Flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home. Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas. A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with. A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities. An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe. About the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML) FHML is committed to health in the broadest sense: from molecule to human, and from healthcare to prevention. We train healthcare professionals and researchers through innovative educational programmes and conduct groundbreaking research in health and well-being. As part of Maastricht UMC+ (MUMC+), our international and interdisciplinary community forms a unique collaboration between university and academic hospital, where education, research, and care come together. About CARIM At CARIM, basic mechanisms as well as early diagnosis and individual risk stratification of cardiovascular disease are studied, allowing faster translation of new research concepts to clinical practice. Our pursuit is to enhance early recognition and prevention of cardiovascular disease, advance therapeutic options, and provide impactful and inspiring mentorship to nurture the growth of young talent and staff in their scientific careers. We value open communication and an inclusive working environment and actively implement our academic recognition & awards program. Interested? Want to know more about this position or what it’s like to work at our university? Reach out to Prof. Judith Sluimer at Judith.sluimer@maastrichtuniversity.nl . Please upload a CV, motivation letter and provide reference letter(s) if available no later than 15 November 2026. You will be informed within 3 weeks after this deadline whether you are invited for an interview including a short presentation of your prior work, likely early December. A reference check is also part of the procedure in phase one. After further selection a lab orientation day will be organized to meet the wider team, and/or an assessment of lab skills. Apply now via the button below. We look forward to getting to know you! About Maastricht University At Maastricht University, we collaboratively seek solutions to help move the world forward. We do this with 23,300 students and 5,400 employees across 5 regional locations, 6 faculties, and more than 70 research institutes. We encourage you to push boundaries and discover new opportunities for yourself and the world around you. Together, we can find the answers for tomorrow. The vacancy is open for internal and external candidates. In case of equal qualifications, internal candidates will be prioritized. At Maastricht University, we prefer to contact potential candidates directly. We therefore kindly ask that no agencies or intermediaries submit offers or approaches. Maastricht University is committed to promoting and nurturing a diverse and inclusive community. We believe that diversity in our staff and student population contributes to the quality of research and education at UM, and strive to enable this through inclusive policies and innovative projects led by teams of staff and students. We encourage you to apply for this position. No Offer Description The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) position in the field of Finite Element Technology for Smooth Problems at the Department of Technical Physics on the Kuopio Campus. The position will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 January 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application by 16 November 2026. Role and salary We are seeking a motivated Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) to work on the development and application of advanced computational methods with a particular focus on finite element technologies for complex continuum and multiphysics problems. The research will combine methodological development, numerical implementation and applications to challenging problems in computational engineering. The research project will be supervised by Assistant Professor Adam Sky from the Department of Technical Physics at the University of Eastern Finland together with Dr. Michael Neunteufel from the Johann Radon Institute for Computational and Applied Mathematics (RICAM) in Linz, Austria. As our new Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), your responsibilities will include the development, mathematical analysis and numerical implementation of finite element methods, as well as the preparation and publication of scientific results. The position may also include a limited amount of teaching-related duties (max. 5% of total working hours), such as developing exercise materials and supervising exercise sessions. The Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will also be expected to participate in scientific exchange through conferences, research visits and collaboration with the participating research groups and institutes. The main duty of the Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for their doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies. The position will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 January 2027 (or as agreed). The position will be filled for a fixed term due to the Doctoral Researcher’s (PhD Student’s) own doctoral dissertation work and studies. A trial period is applied to all new members of the staff. The salary of the position is determined in accordance with the salary system for Finnish universities. The salary comprises two components: a job-related salary element and a personal salary element. For a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), the job-related salary element is based on levels 2–4 of the job requirement level chart for teaching and research staff depending on the stage of the applicant’s doctoral research and postgraduate studies. The personal salary element is 6–50% of the job-related salary element. At the beginning of the employment, the total salary will be approximately EUR 2,710–2,845 /month. Our requirements and expectations We require you to be eligible for postgraduate studies; i.e., to hold a Master’s degree in computational physics and engineering, mathematics, scientific computing, mechanical engineering or a related field, awarded by a university or by a university of applied sciences, or to have completed an applicable study programme abroad which in the awarding country gives eligibility for corresponding postgraduate education meet the student admission criteria for the LUMETO doctoral programme ( Doctoral Programme in Science, Forestry and Technology, website ) have a good command of written and spoken English. Students in the final stages of their Master’s degree may also apply, provided that they complete their degree and deliver a copy of their degree certificate to the faculty by 30 November 2026. Applicants who do not yet have the right to pursue postgraduate studies at the University of Eastern Finland are not required to apply for study rights at the application stage. If the applicant is selected for the position and applies for postgraduate study rights, the selection will be conditional until the right to pursue postgraduate studies in the faculty’s doctoral programme has been granted. The application for postgraduate study rights is submitted through the Studyinfo (Opintopolku) service. Other requirements a strong foundation in mathematics and continuum physics experience in scientific programming, preferably in Python. Experience in the following areas will be considered an advantage finite element methods tensor calculus continuum mechanics generalised continuum theories scientific computing programming in C++, C or Rust. Your benefits You will have access to the university’s staff benefits, including the opportunity for flexible multi-location work extensive occupational health care a broad selection of staff training staff discount on lunch in our campus restaurants, as well as on a range of other services affordable sports services. Please read more in the Work at UEF section on our website . You will have an opportunity to work in meaningful as part of our international, creative, participatory and inclusive academic community. Enjoy your life in Finland! Known for its cleanliness, welfare know-how, modern technology and superb education system, Finland is an exotic and safe country to work in. Please visit the Life in Finland section on our website to learn more. How to apply? Submit your application by using our electronic application form no later than 16 November 2026 by 23:59 (midnight) Finnish time (UTC+2). Please note that you must include the following appendices in your application CV (Template for CV, TENK web page) copies of your academic degree certificates / diplomas, and copies of certificates / diplomas relating to your language proficiency, if not indicated in the academic degree certificates/diplomas a transcript of records a motivation letter (max. 1 page) in which you describe your interest in the position, your background, as well as your career aspirations and your motivation for engaging in doctoral-level research if available (not a pre-requisite), a list of publications ( Instructions, Research Council of Finland, website ) other documents to demonstrate your merits for the position. If your degree certificate is not in English, Finnish, or Swedish, you must provide official English translations of your degree certificate documents. All translations must be issued by the awarding educational institution or an authorized translator. Each page of the official translation must bear the translator's stamp and/or signature. Official translations must be accurate translations of the original documents. Translations made by the applicants themselves will not be accepted. Questions? For further information on the position, please contact Assistant Professor Adam Sky, e-mail: adam.sky@uef.fi . For further information on the application procedure, please contact HR Specialist Iiris Korhonen, e-mail: iiris.korhonen@uef.fi , tel. +358 29 445 8161 or HR Specialist Noora Hämäläinen, e-mail: noora.hamalainen@uef.fi , tel. +358 29 445 8302. Workplace The project will be carried out primarily at the premises of the Foundation for Biosanitary Research and Innovation in Primary Care of the Community of Madrid (FIIBAP), located at Avenida Reina Victoria 21, 6th floor, 28003 Madrid. Functions The selected person will contribute to the launch of the QUALIREHAB programme within the framework of the THCS European Partnership (Joint Transnational Call 2024, https://www.thcspartnership.eu/ ), supporting the integration of evidence-based exercise medicine and rehabilitation into routine healthcare for children, adolescents, and young adults living with chronic conditions. QUALIREHAB is an international implementation research programme that combines implementation science, public health, digital health, multidisciplinary care, and patient engagement to improve lifelong health outcomes. Initially developed and evaluated in the field of congenital heart disease (article available at: https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehae085 , European Heart Journal, 2024), the programme is currently expanding to multiple chronic paediatric conditions, including childhood cancer survivors, chronic kidney disease, cardiovascular diseases, etc. The candidate will work in close collaboration with the QUALIREHAB international consortium to support the implementation, dissemination, and long-term sustainability of the programme across different healthcare systems, starting with Spain, France, and Belgium, with progressive expansion throughout Europe. Contribute to the development, evaluation, and dissemination of implementation strategies that promote preventive rehabilitation in paediatric chronic diseases. Support public health, communication, and stakeholder engagement activities to facilitate the adoption of QUALIREHAB into routine clinical practice. Contribute to European project management, scientific reporting, and dissemination activities, ensuring compliance with the principles of research integrity, ethics, and scientific excellence. Specific functions: Implementation science: Identify barriers and facilitators influencing implementation across different healthcare settings. Contribute to the design and evaluation of implementation strategies and frameworks. Participate in qualitative and mixed-methods implementation research studies. Contribute to the evaluation of implementation outcomes (acceptability, feasibility, adoption, fidelity, sustainability, and scalability). Public health and health policy: Support the development of public health strategies that promote exercise medicine as a preventive intervention for children and young adults living with chronic conditions. Contribute to integrated care pathways and multidisciplinary care models. Participate in drafting policy briefs, implementation recommendations, and healthcare system integration strategies. Organise scientific meetings, workshops, conferences, and stakeholder events. Promote QUALIREHAB through institutional communication and scientific outreach activities. Research management: Contribute to project deliverables and technical reports. Collaborate in monitoring project indicators and implementation outcomes. description: PhD position: High-Throughput Development of Chemical Conversion Treatment for Light Metals Job ID: 1077 Location: Geesthacht/near Hamburg, Germany Application deadline: 17 November, 2026 Aluminium and magnesium alloys are key to lighter vehicles, aircraft, drones and consumer goods but only if they are safe and durable, reliably protected against corrosion. Chemical conversion coatings are one of the most effective and commercially successful ways to do this. They protect the metal and help paint adhere to it. Yet finding better, environmentally friendly formulations is still largely a matter of trial and error. The number of possible formulations is virtually infinite, so we do not test them one by one. At the Department of Electrochemistry and Big Data, we run a robotic high-throughput testing platform combined with machine learning for AI-assisted discoveries. We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a PhD student in the quickly developing field of high-throughput and robotic experimentation in materials science. The position is part-time (19,5 h/week) and will be located in Hereon's main campus, in Geesthacht (near Hamburg). We value diversity and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply. Your tasks - Develop and validate experimental methods for the accelerated screening of chemical conversion treatment formulations - Translate these methods into automated high-throughput workflows on our existing robotic testing platform - Work side by side with our computational scientists to build large, machine-readable datasets for AI-assisted discovery - Uncover the mechanisms behind effective adhesion promotion and corrosion protection, and turn them into design rules for next-generation coatings - Publish your results in leading journals, present at international conferences, write project reports, and contribute to open, FAIR datasets Your profile - A completed master's degree in chemistry, electrochemistry, materials science, computational materials science or a related field - Solid experimental skills in chemical laboratories and confidence in quantitative data analysis using appropriate software - Experience with corrosion protection, including chemical conversion coatings for light alloys (Mg, Al or Zn) - Experience with electronic lab notebooks, FAIR data, databases or machine learning - Curiosity about automation and AI, and motivation to work at the interface of experiment and computation - Very good English, knowledge of the German language is preferred but not mandatory, we support language learning Content-related enquiries regarding this position can be directed to Sviatlana.Lamaka(at)hereon.de. Our offer - A research topic with real industrial relevance, at the frontier of lab automation and Al-driven materials discovery - A doctorate awarded by Hamburg University of Technology, TUHH, our partner university - Access to state-of-the-art (robotic) labs, unique scientific and technical infrastructure - Access to a large international research and industrial network - Funding for conferences, summer schools and courses needed or research stays - An exciting job in a research center with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations - International Welcome Office with guest accommodation - 6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's Day - Social benefits according to the collective agreement of the public service and remuneration up to EG 13 (according to EntgO Bund) - Very good work-life balance; options for mobile and flexible work - A green campus on the Elbe River, well-connected with Hamburg (public transport), subsidy for the Deutschlandticket if certain conditions are met (job ticket), charging facilities for electric vehicles - PhD Buddy Program - Family-friendly company policy with childcare facilities, e.g. nursery/kindergarten close to the company - Operational Health Management, e.g. Employee Assistance Program (EAP) - Corporate Benefits - A varied offer in the canteen on campus Severely disabled persons and those equaling severely disabled persons who are equally suitable for the position will be considered preferentially within the framework of legal requirements. Interested? Then we are looking forward to receiving your comprehensive application documents (cover letter, CV, transcripts, certificates, etc.) indicating the reference number code 1077 until 03 November, 2026. Apply now! https://jobs2.hereon.de/job/PhD-position-High-Throughput-Development-of-Chemical-Conversion-Treatment-for-Light-Metals/1077-en_US/

description: 128 Application Deadline: 17 November 2026. Applications are now open for th e DSTI-NRF Policy Fellowship Programme. The National Research Foundation (NRF), in partnership with the Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI), invites eligible early- and mid-career researchers to apply for the second cohort of the DSTI–NRF Policy Fellowship Programme. The programme aims to strengthen the relationship between research and policymaking by placing researchers within designated host institutions, where they can contribute to policy development, analysis and implementation. Through these placements, Fellows will gain practical policy experience while supporting the use of research evidence to inform decision-making and address South Africa’s socio-economic and developmental challenges. Building on the 2024 pilot programme, Cohort 2 offers a structured fellowship experience that combines a host institution placement with NRF-coordinated policy engagement, training and capacity development, including opportunities for international exposure and cross-sectoral networking. Areas of support The programme supports research and policy engagement across a range of thematic areas, including: Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) policy and governance; Energy, climate change and just transition; Digital transformation, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies; Urban development, local government and spatial planning; Health, public health and health systems; Agriculture, food systems and rural development; Environment, sustainability and natural resources; Social development, education and human capital; Public administration, governance and institutional reform; and International relations, science diplomacy and partnerships. Applicants will be required to select up to three potential host institutions from the options provided in the application process. Applicants are encouraged to consider the location of their preferred hosts, as regular physical attendance may be required. Requirements This opportunity is open to early- and mid-career individuals who obtained their doctoral degree within the past 10 years. Applicants must be South African citizens or permanent residents. In exceptional, well-justified cases, non-South African applicants may also be considered, subject to the programme’s limit of no more than 10% of all Fellowship recipients. Applicants must also be registered or employed, on a permanent or fixed-term basis, at an NRF-recognised research institution, or be able to secure such an affiliation before taking up the grant. Eligible institutions include public universities, science councils, museums and national facilities in South Africa. Fellowship duration and funding Successful applicants will receive fellowship funding for a maximum period of 24 months, with an annual award value ranging from R240,000 to R320,000 . Fellows will participate in both the host institution placement and the NRF-coordinated policy engagement and capacity development programme. Successful applicants will be required to agree to defined responsibilities, deliverables, participation requirements and reporting obligations. How to apply Applicants must complete the application for the DSTI–NRF Policy Fellowship Programme – Cohort 2 on this link: https://forms.gle/gUDuvrmPRFeuRmbK9 , and attach the required supporting documents in PDF format. Compulsory attachments include: ID/Passport copy Proof of doctoral qualification; and For currently employed applicants, written confirmation from their employer or institution supporting their participation and availability to meet the fellowship’s placement, training, policy engagement and travel commitments. For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the DSTI-NRF Policy Fellowship Programme

No Offer Description We invite applications for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow position in Marine Plankton Biology available at the Department of Biosciences, University of Oslo. The postdoctoral position is affiliated with the ToxANoWa II project (Toxic microalgae in Norwegian waters — Providing knowledge and methods necessary for monitoring of algal toxins and algae harmful to fish), which is funded by FHF (the Norwegian Seafood Research Fund). The project aims to generate knowledge on algal toxins harmful to fish, their production and toxic effects in Norwegian coastal waters. Another aim is to develop fast and improved methods to monitor toxins and algae causing mortality to farmed fish. ToxANoWa II is structured into five scientific work packages: 1) Characterizing microalgal communities, algal toxins, and metabolomes in field samples from HAB-affected areas; 2) Toxicity, toxins, and metabolomes in cultures of potentially fish-toxic algae from Norwegian waters; 3) Potential screening methods for monitoring algae and their toxins in relation to fish mortality; 4) Toxicity of C. leadbeateri cultures and leadbeaterins in fish and gill cells; and 5) Producing toxin reference materials. UiO and the candidate will take part in all work packages except the last. The project is a collaborative effort involving partners from Norway (Veterinary institute and University of Oslo), Denmark (DTU), Canada (NRC), and New Zealand (Cawthron). The candidate will collaborate with all partners in the project. A research stay abroad will be encouraged. Some of the work will take place at the UiO owned Biological station in Drøbak, and some at the Veterinary institute at Ås. description: 24 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Itä-Suomen yliopisto Department The Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology, School of Computing Research Field Computer science Engineering Technology » Information technology Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 17 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Finland Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? No Offer Description The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in the field of Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data at the School of Computing on the Kuopio campus. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application by 17 November 2026. Role and salary The demand for minerals required for energy transition and digitalisation is expanding mining faster than our ability to understand its impacts. MINE-THE-GAP (website) , funded by the European Research Council (ERC), combines satellite imagery, mining data reports, and AI to map mining activities and their impacts worldwide and provide the information needed for more transparent and sustainable mining. We are seeking three motivated Doctoral Researchers (PhD Students) to join the project, each leading their own thesis on mapping different aspects of mining. As part of the MINE-THE-GAP team, you will, as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), have the opportunity to apply your data science and programming skills to a global sustainability challenge and to become an expert in handling large Earth observation datasets and scalable AI. We offer three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in a research group with strong international visibility. You will receive hands-on training in the processing of large Earth observation and spatial datasets, as well as in scalable AI methods, developing highly sought-after skills for careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations. The position provides opportunities for international collaboration and research visits abroad through an extensive network of partner institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Monash University Indonesia, and the University of Melbourne. You will benefit from close supervision, mentoring, and a supportive team environment, along with dedicated funding for conference participation, workshops, and scientific publications. One Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will be recruited for each of the following three research topics: mining land use: semantic segmentation of satellite images to map mining areas (e.g., open pits, waste rock piles, tailings dams) mining waste: predicting terrain height changes from radar and optical satellite image time series to estimate mining waste minerals and commodities: image classification with multispectral and hyperspectral data to identify the minerals and commodities of mining sites. Within your chosen research topic, you will build, train, and validate scalable deep learning and computer vision models using large, multi-modal Earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, LiDAR, hyperspectral). You will work closely with the principal investigator, Victor Maus, postdoctoral researchers, and international collaborators, publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to open science. Your main duty as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for the doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). The positions will be filled for a fixed term due to the Doctoral Researcher’s (PhD Student’s) own doctoral dissertation work and studies. A trial period is applied to all new members of the staff. The salary of the position is determined in accordance with the salary system for Finnish universities. The salary comprises two components: a job-related salary element and a personal salary element. For a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), the job-related salary element is based on levels 2–4 of the job requirement level chart for teaching and research staff depending on the stage of the applicant’s doctoral research and postgraduate studies. The personal salary element is 6–50% of the job-related salary element. At the beginning of the employment, the total salary will be approximately EUR 2,710–2,845 /month. Our requirements and expectations We require you to be eligible for postgraduate studies; i.e., to hold a Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Geoinformatics, Statistics, or a related field) awarded by a university or by a university of applied sciences, or to have completed an applicable study programme abroad which in the awarding country gives eligibility for corresponding postgraduate education meet the student admission criteria for the LUMETO doctoral programme ( Doctoral Programme in Science, Forestry and Technology, website ) have a good command of written and spoken English. Students in the final stages of their Master’s degree may also apply provided that they complete their degree and deliver a copy of their degree certificate to the faculty by 15 December 2026. Applicants who do not yet have the right to pursue postgraduate studies at the University of Eastern Finland are not required to apply for study rights at the application stage. If the applicant is selected for the position and applies for postgraduate study rights, the selection will be conditional until the right to pursue postgraduate studies in the faculty’s doctoral programme has been granted. The application for postgraduate study rights is submitted through the Studyinfo (Opintopolku) service. Other requirements good programming skills (e.g., Python/R) interest in machine learning and spatial data. The following will be considered an advantage experience with machine learning or deep learning (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) or strong motivation to learn these skills experience with Earth observation or geospatial data, desirable, but we encourage anyone with a strong willingness to learn to apply experience with cloud computing or collaborative software development (e.g., GitHub) is also welcome. Your benefits You will have access to the university’s staff benefits, including the opportunity for flexible multi-location work excellent opportunities for professional development and continuous learning extensive occupational health care a broad selection of staff training staff discount on lunch in our campus restaurants, as well as on a range of other services affordable sports services. Please read more in the Work at UEF section on our website . You will have an opportunity to work in meaningful as part of our international, creative, participatory and inclusive academic community. Enjoy your life in Finland! Known for its cleanliness, welfare know-how, modern technology and superb education system, Finland is an exotic and safe country to work in. Please visit the Life in Finland section on our website to learn more. How to apply? Submit your application by using our electronic application form no later than 17 November 2026 by 23:59 (midnight) Finnish time (UTC+2). Please note that you must include the following appendices in your application CV (Template for CV, TENK web page) a list of publications (Instructions, Research Council of Finland Web page) copies of your academic degree certificates / diplomas, and copies of certificates / diplomas relating to your language proficiency, if not indicated in the academic degree certificates/diplomas a transcript of records a motivation letter (max. 1 page) describing your interest in the position and research project, your background, as well as your career aspirations and your motivation for engaging in doctoral-level research. In the cover letter, indicate your preferred topic(s), for example, by ranking the topics in order of preference or specifying whether you are applying for one or multiple topics. External evaluation will be used in the recruitment process. If your degree certificate is not in English, Finnish, or Swedish, you must provide official English translations of your degree certificate documents. All translations must be issued by the awarding educational institution or an authorized translator. Each page of the official translation must bear the translator's stamp and/or signature. Official translations must be accurate translations of the original documents. Translations made by the applicants themselves will not be accepted. Questions? For further information on the position, please contact Professor Markku Tukiainen, email: markku.tukiainen@uef.fi , tel. +358 29 445 3653. For further information on the application procedure, please contact HR Specialist Iiris Korhonen, email: iiris.korhonen@uef.fi , tel. +358 29 4458161 or HR Specialist Noora Hämäläinen, email: noora.hamalainen@uef.fi , tel. +358 29 4458302. Haemme kolmea väitöskirjatutkijaa Itä-Suomen yliopistolle. Tehtävät sijoittuvat luonnontieteiden, metsätieteiden ja tekniikan tiedekuntaan tietojenkäsittelytieteiden laitokselle Kuopion kampukselle. Tehtävät alkavat 1.2.2027 (tai sopimuksen mukaan) ja ne täytetään kolmen vuoden määräajaksi. Tehtävissä tehtäväkohtainen palkanosa on vaativuustasoluokittelussa tasoilla 2–4. Lisäksi maksetaan henkilökohtaiseen suoriutumiseen perustuvaa palkanosaa, joka on 6–50 % tehtäväkohtaisesta palkanosasta. Tehtävissä edellytetään hyvää englannin kielen taitoa. ​ Lue tarkemmat tiedot tehtävistä ja hakuohjeet yllä olevasta englanninkielisestä ilmoituksesta. Jätäthän hakemuksesi englanniksi. Hakuaika tehtäviin päättyy 17.11.2026.
