description: 31 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company University of Oslo Research Field Computer science Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Positions PhD Positions Application Deadline 18 Nov 2026 - 23:00 (Europe/Oslo) Country Norway Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Hours Per Week 37.5 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Integreat - the Norwegian Centre for Knowledge-driven Machine Learning is seeking a motivated PhD candidate to join our interdisciplinary research centre at the University of Oslo, Norway. You will be part of a dynamic group of early career researchers, supervised by senior experts, collaborating across disciplines to tackle fundamental challenges through innovative methods, theory and critical analysis. Vision-language models (VLMs) can name what is in a picture, but they often miss what is happening in it. Shown a park scene, a model may list "a dog", "a Frisbee" and "a park" and still fail to say that the dog is leaping to catch the Frisbee mid-air. The same gap shows up when a model misreads a symbolic painting or gives a vague description of a medical image. More training data does not close this gap, because the models have no explicit representation of how the objects in a scene relate to each other. This project gives VLMs that representation. You will develop panoptic scene graphs, in which every object and background region in an image becomes a node and the edges encode spatial, semantic and relational context. The graphs are built from superpixels rather than the fixed square patches used in standard vision transformers. Superpixels follow object boundaries, so the nodes of the graph are meaningful from the start. The project builds directly on our recent work on superpixel tokenization for vision transformers (ECCV Workshops 2024, NeurIPS 2025). description: 6 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company NTNU Norwegian University of Science and Technology Department Department of Materials Science and Engineering Research Field Engineering » Materials engineering Technology » Materials technology Engineering » Mechanical engineering Researcher Profile Recognised Researcher (R2) Positions Other Positions Application Deadline 19 Nov 2026 - 23:59 (Europe/Oslo) Country Norway Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Hours Per Week 37,5 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description This is NTNU NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim. At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world. You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here. About the position We are seeking a researcher with a background in welding, metal additive manufacturing or a related area of physical metallurgy for an approximately one-year position within SFI PhysMet (Centre for Sustainable and Competitive Metallurgical and Manufacturing Industry; www.ntnu.edu/physmet ) at the Department of Materials Science and Engineering, NTNU. The position offers the opportunity to take a leading role in an experimental study of low transformation temperature (LTT) alloys. You will build on existing specimens and recent results, shape the remaining investigations and lead the preparation of a full-length journal manuscript together with the project team. We welcome applicants who enjoy connecting microstructural observations with physical metallurgy understanding and transforming experimental findings into clear scientific conclusions. Your immediate leader is Head of Department. About the job LTT alloys undergo transformation from austenite to martensite at relatively low temperatures. The associated volume expansion can counteract thermal contraction and offers a route to managing residual stresses in welding and additive manufacturing. Understanding how processing conditions and repeated thermal cycles affect their microstructure is important for assessing their potential in these applications. The experimental work has so far focused on directed energy deposition (DED). Single tracks, double tracks and small cuboids have been printed from three LTT alloys. Initial characterisation has included sectioning and light optical microscopy (LOM) to examine printing defects and dilution, Vickers hardness measurements, and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) on selected specimens, including reconstruction of prior-austenite grains. More recently, cubes have also been produced by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) using two of the alloy powders. Microstructural characterisation of these specimens by LOM is currently in progress. You will bring the existing and emerging results together to investigate the relationships between processing, microstructure, printing quality and hardness. The work will include identifying the most valuable scientific questions, establishing where the DED and LPBF results can be meaningfully compared, and completing focused complementary characterisation. The main outcome should be one or more full-length manuscripts prepared and submitted to a relevant peer-reviewed journal. Duties of the position One of the main objectives of SFI PhysMet is to explore and develop innovative processing and joining methods with enhanced sustainability and competitiveness. You will contribute to this aim through the following activities: Review, consolidate and document the existing specimens, processing information and characterisation results. Define a focused plan for completing the study, identifying the additional analyses or experiments needed to support its scientific conclusions. Carry out and analyse complementary microstructural characterisation and strength property measurements in collaboration with the project team. Investigate the effects of alloy composition, processing conditions, dilution and repeated thermal cycles on microstructure and hardness, using the available evidence. Develop a scientifically justified comparison of the DED and LPBF results for the alloys studied by both processes. Lead the interpretation of the results and the preparation and submission of at least one full-length journal manuscript in collaboration with the project team. Communicate the findings through project meetings and relevant scientific conferences and document the data and analysis procedures for future use. You will work closely with colleagues and partners within SFI PhysMet. Research visits and participation in relevant conferences are encouraged as opportunities to strengthen the study, exchange knowledge and expand your scientific network. Required selection criteria A PhD in materials science and engineering, metallurgy, welding technology, mechanical engineering or a closely related discipline, or documented scientific qualifications at an equivalent level. Relevant experimental research experience in welding metallurgy, metal additive manufacturing or a related field involving solidification and phase transformations in metallic materials. Hands-on experience with metallographic sample preparation and microstructural characterisation of metallic materials, by light optical and electron microscopy methods. Demonstrated ability to analyse experimental data independently and relate processing conditions, microstructure and material properties. Experience in scientific writing, demonstrated by relevant publications, and the ability to take a leading role in manuscript preparation. Excellent written and oral English communication skills. Preferred selection criteria We welcome applicants with different combinations of the following experience: Experience with DED and/or LPBF, including interpretation of processing parameters and thermal histories. Experience with steel metallurgy, including knowledge of LTT alloys, martensitic transformations or transformation-related effects in welding and additive manufacturing. Experience acquiring and/or analysing EBSD data, particularly reconstruction of prior-austenite grains. Experience with quantitative optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), image analysis and Vickers hardness testing. Experience assessing weld or additive manufacturing defects, dilution and the effects of repeated thermal cycling. Skills in quantitative data analysis and scientific visualisation using Python, MATLAB or comparable tools. Familiarity with thermodynamic or phase-transformation modelling to support experimental interpretation. Personal characteristics Curious and analytical, with sound scientific judgement. Able to work independently, set priorities and bring a focused research study to completion. Careful and systematic in experimental work, data management and reporting. Open to sharing ideas and collaborating across research groups and disciplines. Motivated to communicate research through publications and scientific presentations. Emphasis will be placed on personal and interpersonal qualities. We offer An established experimental foundation and the opportunity to shape the remaining research and lead its scientific publication. Exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment. Collaboration in a strong team of research fellows from NTNU and SINTEF in addition to industry partners in SFI PhysMet An open and inclusive work environment with dedicated colleagues Favourable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund E mployee benefits Excellent research infrastructure for experiments and modelling Salary and conditions As a researcher (code 1109) you are paid depending on qualifications and seniority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund. The period of employment is one year. An early start is preferred, with the starting date to be agreed with the successful applicant. The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants , and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU. After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. About the application Your application and supporting documentation must be in English. The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English. Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request. If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result. Your application must include: A short cover letter explaining your motivation, relevant expertise and approach to completing the study, including your earliest possible starting date. A CV, relevant certificates and a list of publications. Relevant diplomas and transcripts, including documentation of your doctoral degree or equivalent scientific qualifications. A copy of your doctoral thesis, or equivalent documentation of scientific competence. Up to five relevant scientific works, published or unpublished, that you would like to be considered. Names and contact information for three referees. It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for documentation of your competence. Joint work will also be considered. If it is difficult to identify your specific input to a joint project, you must include evidence of your contributions. In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized. NTNU is obliged by the evaluation criteria for research quality in accordance with The San Fransisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and The obligations in the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment ( CoARA) on responsible assessment of research and recognition of a wider range of academic contributions to science and society. This means that we will pay particular attention to the quality and academic range demonstrated by your scientific work to date. We will also pay attention to research leadership and participation in research projects. Your scientific work from the last five years will be given the most weight. Your application will be considered by a committee at the department. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview. General information Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful . We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes. A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation . You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted. For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality. If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Associate Professor Tomáš Mánik, email: tomas.manik@ntnu.no . If you have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact HR Advisor Marie Kristiansen, e-mail marie.kristiansen@ntnu.no Application deadline: 19.11.2026 The city of Trondheim is a modern European city with a rich cultural scene. Trondheim is the innovation capital of Norway with a population of 200,000. The Norwegian welfare state, including healthcare, schools, kindergartens and overall equality, is probably the best of its kind in the world. Professional subsidized day-care for children is easily available. Furthermore, Trondheim offers great opportunities for education (including international schools) and possibilities to enjoy nature, culture and family life and has low crime rates and clean air quality. NTNU - knowledge for a better world NTNU - knowledge for a better world The Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) creates knowledge for a better world and solutions that can change everyday life. Department of Materials Science and Engineering We are Norway's leading educational and research environment in materials engineering, materials chemistry and materials science. In collaboration with business and industry, we are a driving force for the development of innovative materials as well as new applications and manufacturing processes. Activities in our disciplines are vital for the green shift. The Department of Materials Science and Engineering is one of seven departments in the Faculty of Natural Sciences . description: 5 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Politécnico de Leiria Department CDRSP Research Field Engineering » Civil engineering Engineering » Materials engineering Engineering » Mechanical engineering Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Positions Other Positions Application Deadline 19 Nov 2026 - 23:59 (Europe/London) Country Portugal Type of Contract Other Type of Contract Extra Information research fellowship contract Job Status Other Job Status Extra Information 12 months, eventually renewable Hours Per Week 35 Offer Starting Date 6 Nov 2026 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Other EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description University of Leiria and Oeste is now opening applications for 1 (one) research fellowship (BI) within the project “SR-Facade - Desenvolvimento de Sistema de Revestimento de Fachadas de Edifícios com Painéis Intermutáveis (CENTRO2030-FEDER-02956700)”, financed by the Centro Regional Programme (Centro 2030) _PT2030, through the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), under the following conditions: . SCIENTIFIC AREA: Mechanical Engineering, materials Engineering and Civil Engineering. . RECIPIENTS: Holders of a master’s degree Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering or materials Engineering who are PhD students in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering or materials Engineering or related areas or who are enrolled in courses that do not confer an academic degree in association with a Research Unit (UI). . DURATION: 12 months, eventually renewable until the end of the project or the maximum duration for this research fellowship type. If the research fellowship is awarded to a candidate enrolled in courses that do not confer an academic degree, the maximum duration is 12 months (non-renewable). The fellowship is due to start in 2026/12. . WORK PLAN: Conception and Design; Prototype Construction; Testing and Validation; Dissemination and Promotion; and Technical Management . WORKPLACE AND SCIENTIFIC SUPERVISION: The work will be developed at the Centre for Rapid and Sustained Product Development from University of Leiria and Oeste (CDRSP-ULO), under the supervision of PhD professor: Florindo José Mendes Gaspar. . GRANT FINANTIAL COMPONENTS: Monthly maintenance subsidy, in the amount of € 1359,64 according to the FCT, I.P. ( https://www.fct.pt/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Tabela-de-Valores-SMM-202… . To this amount is added the monthly amount referring to the Voluntary Social Security, if applicable, in accordance with the conditions defined in the Statute of Research Fellows. The scholarship holder will benefit from Personal Accident Insurance during the course of the scholarship. . PAYMENT: The maintenance stipend will be monthly processed, through bank transfer, to the account identified by the research fellow. . ACTIVITY SCHEME: Exclusivity, according to the applicable legislation. . EVALUATION PANEL: The jury responsible for the applications evaluation will be constituted by PhD Professors: Florindo José Mendes Gaspar (president), Rui Miguel Barreiros Ruben and António Mário Henriques Pereira (effective members); Pedro José da Silva Carreira and Nelson Simões Oliveira (substitute members). . APPLICATION DEADLINE: november 06, 2026 to november 19, 2026. . SELECTION METHOD AND EVALUATION CRITERIA: The evaluation will be made through curriculum analysis and possible interview, and will focus on the merit of the candidate, where they will be considered and weighted according to the following: a) Academic Qualification (AQ): final grade of master's degree b) Professional/Academic Experience (PAE) • Has excellent professional/academic experience – 20 values. • Has very good professional/academic experience – 17 values. • Has good professional/academic experience – 14 values. • Has enough professional/academic experience – 10 values. • Has insufficient professional/academic experience – 2 values. • No mention of professional/academic practice – 0 values. c) Specific knowledge (SK): Experience and knowledge in the development of facade cladding systems, including modeling, material selection, development, performance evaluation (physical and mechanical), and application in manufacturing processes. •Excellent knowledge - 20 values. •High knowledge - 15 values. •Medium knowledge - 10 values. •Low level of knowledge - 5 values. •No knowledge - 0 values. with the final grade FG = [AQ*0.5 + PAE*0.2 + SK* 0.3]. If the jury decides by reasoned deliberation, the three first classified in the curriculum analysis will be invited for an interview (INT), with the final grade (FG) = [FG*0.8 + INT*0.2]. Candidates who, at the end of the assessment, obtain a classification of less than 9.5 will be excluded from the contest. Observation: If the candidate(s) with foreign qualifications(s) do not present, during the application phase, the recognition of the degree or foreign diploma and the classification conversion to the Portuguese scale, the jury defines the conversion only for the application purposes based on the rules of the legal regime applicable to the recognition of foreign degrees and diplomas or, when not possible, applies the minimal classification of 10 points. Note that foreign academic degrees need to be registered by a Portuguese institution, in accordance with Decree-law no. 66/2018, dated August 16th, and Ordinance no. 33/2019, dated January 25th. The presentation of the certificate is mandatory for signing the contract. More information can be obtained at: https://www.dges.gov.pt/pt/pagina/reconhecimento?plid=374 . ELIGIBILITY OF CANDIDATES: Without prejudice to the applicable rules to each type of research fellowship, the following candidates are eligible: a) National citizens or citizens of other member states of the European Union; b) Third-party states citizens; c) Stateless persons; d) Beneficiaries of political refugee status. . SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS: Applications must be submitted through https://recrutamento.ipleiria.pt/processos-ativos/bolseiros/concurso?re… by clicking the "submit application" button, filling out and submitting the application form accompanied by the following documents: - Document(s) proving the ownership of the academic degree(s) and/or required application diploma(s), preferably with the final average and curricular units’ classification. Candidates with foreign qualifications must prove their academic degree and foreign diploma in the terms of the Decree-law no. 66/2018, dated August 16th. These documents can be dismissed during the application phase, by submitting a declaration of honour available in the application form, which can only attest to facts that occurred prior to the application, with the verification of this condition occurring only in the contract signing phase; - Document proving the enrolment and registration in the study cycle in courses that do not confer an academic degree (optional presentation in the application stage, which in turn is a mandatory element when contracting the research grant); - Updated candidate Curriculum Vitae; - Document(s) supporting other evaluation parameter(s) indicated in the announcement; - Other certifications and/or other documents considered relevant by the candidate. . RESULTS | DISCLOSURE AND COMPLAINTS: The jury will send to the candidates, by e-mail, the provisional results of the evaluation (presented in the form of the minutes resulting from the evaluation process) within 90 working days after the application deadline. After this disclosure, candidates have 10 working days to pronounce, if they wish, in the appropriate form available in the institutional webpage, under the terms of the administrative procedure code (CPA). The final decision will be taken within a maximum period of 60 working days after the conclusion of the previous hearing of interested parties, of which a complaint can be filed within 15 working days, after notification, to the highest executive body of the University of Leiria and Oeste. Within the scope of the research fellowship award procedure, if the final ordering list, duly approved, contains a number of approved candidates higher than the number of research fellowships to be filled, an internal recruitment reserve is always created, which can be used when there is need for occupation due to withdrawal of the scholarship holder, under the terms of the CPA, to be used during the eligibility of the project. . APPLICABLE LEGISLATION AND REGULATION: Research Fellowship Holder statute, approved by Law no. 40/2004, dated August 18th, in its current wording; Regulation n.º 152/2021, with amendment introduced by Regulation nº. 548/2022 dated June 8th (Polytechnic of Leiria Regulation for Studentships and Fellowships). description: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications. About the Role Seeking an exceptional Mechanical Engineer to execute high-level mechanical maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs across all Tupande Soko factories and reduce operational downtime for our processing operations. Responsibilities Hands-on Mechanical Maintenance & Repair Execute hands-on mechanical repairs on critical processing machinery to ensure operational continuity across all factory locations. Troubleshoot complex mechanical equipment failures directly, providing on-the-spot technical interventions when standard maintenance staff or vendors are unavailable. Perform routine and deep-dive mechanical overhauls, component replacements, and structural alignments on heavy plant machinery. Preventive Maintenance & Execution Physically execute mechanical preventative maintenance schedules and job plans assigned via the CMMS. Inspect, adjust, and overhaul mechanical assemblies (such as gearboxes, pumps, hydraulic rams, pneumatic lines, conveyors, and bearings). Track and provide direct data to the Lead Engineer on mechanical asset conditions, failure modes, and component wear rates. Machinery Focus & Asset Care Act as the core mechanical technical intervention specialist for Soko factory machinery repairs and maintenance. Ensure all soko machinery is in a good performance state. Conduct technical repairs on industrial dehydrators, macadamia processing systems, and industrial-level biochar production equipment. Verify and list precise mechanical specifications for machines, spare parts, and consumables requested by factory teams. Workforce Mentorship & TPM Support Mentor and model best-practice mechanical repair techniques during direct interaction with factory staff to elevate technical standards Assist in delivering TPM (Total Productive Maintenance) maintenance training for machine operators specifically regarding mechanical checks, cleaning, and precision lubrication Coach operators on identifying early mechanical warning signs like abnormal vibrations, heat, or noise Safety, Food Safety, and Regulation Ensure all maintenance activities comply with safe systems of work: permit to work, LOTO, confined space, and relevant Kenyan regulatory requirements (KEBS, DOSH, NEMA) Maintain HACCP-required equipment records for food-contact assets; lead the maintenance function's contribution to food safety audits Champion a zero-harm safety culture on the shop floor; report hazards and quickly close out structural or machine risk issues Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You'll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You'll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Technical skills: Degree or Higher Diploma in Mechanical Engineering or appropriate engineering field Active registration/membership as an engineer or technical practitioner in Kenya Preventive/predictive maintenance programme design and implementation Experience with avocado oil machinery repairs and maintenance preferred Experience with industrial dehydrators, macadamia processing, and industrial level biochar production preferred Ability to utilize CMMS software (SAP PM, Maximo, Limble, etc.) to close work orders and log technical data Deep mechanical fault-finding and root cause analysis on industrial plant equipment Proficiency in mechanical drawings, pneumatics, hydraulics, and welding/fabrication techniques Knowledge: Food safety management systems and HACCP requirements as applied to plant maintenance Kenyan occupational health and safety legislation (OSHA, DOSH requirements) TPM (Total Productive Maintenance) or World Class Manufacturing principles Kenyan regulatory environment for food manufacturing (KEBS, relevant standards) Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Rukanga, Kenya Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 2 years Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya. Application Deadline 20 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization's mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. description: 30 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Wageningen University & Research Research Field Biological sciences » Zoology Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 20 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Insects are exposed to a diverse range of infectious viruses throughout their lives. In recent years, advances in largescale sequencing technologies have accelerated virus discovery, revealing a rich and diverse resident assemblage of viruses or 'virome' in insects, including covert viral infections that appear asymptomatic. To date it is unclear how such a virome impacts insect life. In this project you will investigate how the resident virome impacts insect immune responses and fitness and thereby influences interactions with and effects of incoming virus infections. First, you will define the virome in several lepidopteran species and determine how the virome impacts insect life history traits and responses to incoming infections. In a next step, you will study in detail vertical transmission of the virome and investigate how the virome affects transgenerational immune priming (TgIP), a process whereby incoming infections lead to immune protection against secondary infections in the next generation. By integrating virome sequencing and experimental infections with -omics approaches, microscopy, and gene editing tools, you will reveal fundamental mechanisms of insect immunity and virus-induced TgIP and the impact of the virome thereon. This PhD project is part of a larger Vici project, funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO). As such, you will closely collaborate with another PhD student and a postdoc in this project, working on related questions. As a PhD candidate, you will contribute to fundamental science in the context of insect virology. In addition, you will participate in cursory teaching of the chair group. You will be embedded in the Laboratory of Virology and be co-supervised by the Laboratory of Entomology. In addition, you will collaborate with (inter)national colleagues from both in- and outside Wageningen University & Research. Your duties and responsibilities include: Designing and executing experiments with insects and viruses, measuring life history traits, immune traits and responses to virus infections; Investigating virus transmission using hybridization techniques and confocal microscopy; Analysing complex datasets involving genomics, transcriptomics, small RNA sequencing and proteomics; Teaching in courses and supervising BSc and MSc thesis students; Writing and presenting research at/in internationally renowned conferences/journals. You will work here You will work within the Insect Virology group, as part of the NWO Vici project ‘Invisible influencers: How hidden virus infections shape insect life’ led by Dr. Vera Ros. The project is aimed at disentangling how the insect’s virome impacts insect immune responses, fitness and behaviour, and thereby influences interactions with and effects of incoming virus infections. The Insect Virology group is part of the chair group Laboratory of Virology and research in Insect Virology focuses on multiple aspects of insect-virus interactions including mechanisms behind viral manipulation of insect behaviour, virus discovery, covert virus infections (i.e. infections without clear symptoms) in insects and the use of viruses for biological control of insect pests. You will be supervised by Dr. Vera Ros, Dr. Astrid Bryon (both WUR Laboratory of Virology) and Prof. Bregje Wertheim (WUR Laboratory of Entomology). In addition, you will also be embedded in the PE&RC graduate school ( Home | PE&RC ), which will allow you to follow a wide variety of training courses and will provide support during your academic journey. The Laboratory of Virology is part of the Plant Sciences Group of Wageningen University. It is located at the Wageningen Campus in the Radix building. We provide virology teaching at Wageningen University within BSc and MSc programs across various disciplines. The Virology chair group comprises around 35 members, including research/teaching staff, technicians, PhD candidates, postdocs and visiting researchers. Each year, an average of 25 BSc and MSc students undertake their final-year thesis research within Virology. The Virology group conducts fundamental research into plant viruses, insect viruses and arboviruses. Where possible, the knowledge generated is translated into applications aimed at improving food production and human and animal health. Where to apply Website https://www.academictransfer.com/en/jobs/365148/phd-insect-virology-impact-of-t… Requirements Specific Requirements You are an enthusiastic, highly motivated and curiosity-driven person, with a solid background in entomology and insect pathology, with a focus on interactions between insects and micro-organisms/viruses. You have a strong interest in molecular mechanisms underlying virus-insect interactions and in ecological aspects of insect immunity. You are a driven, eager-to-learn person, strong in analytical and conceptual thinking, and can carry out experiments with precision. You are well able to work independently, but also enjoy working closely together in a multidisciplinary team. You also possess: A successfully completed MSc degree in biology or a related field Excellent skills in molecular biological techniques Basic knowledge of bioinformatics A proven ability in designing and performing experiments with insects Ability to work in an international research team in a collaborative spirit Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken, and experience with scientific writing For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here . Additional Information Benefits Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment . A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: Partially paid parental leave; working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%; excellent pension scheme. In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team. The gross salary for the first year is € 3.204,- per month rising to € 4.051,- in the fourth year in according to the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (scale P). This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help. You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment. Selection process For more information about the position, please contact Dr. Vera Ros, Associate Professor, via +31-317-484461 or email: vera.ros@wur.nl . Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Noorien Abbas, Corporate Recruiter, via vacaturemeldingen.psg@wur.nl . Ready to apply? You can apply directly using the apply button on the vacancy page on our website which will allow us to process your personal information with your approval. Only applications submitted through our website will be considered. To apply, please send the following documents ( max. 3 pages in total ): Complete and up-to-date curriculum vitae (max. 2 pages); Motivation letter (max. 1 page). The maximum length of the documents must not exceed 3 pages. If it exceeds, applications will not be considered. Additional files such as grades, transcripts and recommendation letters are not required during this stage and will not be considered. You can apply up to and including November 20, 2026. The first interviews are scheduled for the first two weeks of December, 2026. Additional information form For this position, you must fill in a mandatory form which will allow us to have a comprehensive view of your qualifications and better assess your fit for it. You can access the form using the link below: PhD Insect Virology: the impact of the insect’s virome on insect immunity and fitness – Fill out form Your prompt response will ensure that your application continues to move forward in the evaluation process. We assure you that the information provided will be kept confidential and used solely for this application process. Welcome, safe, and valued Wageningen University & Research (WUR) highly values diversity and inclusion because we believe that different insights lead to innovative solutions. We create a work environment where everyone feels welcome, safe, and appreciated, regardless of background, identity, or experience. Together, we are building a culture where everyone's unique contribution adds to the success of our organization. Additional comments Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees. Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account, dual career programs or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands. description: 25 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Lunds universitet Department Lund University Research Field Physics » Other Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 20 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Sweden Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description The Nuclear Structure Group at the Division of Particle and Nuclear Physics at Lund University is seeking a skilled and highly motivated PhD student to work on upcycling state-of-the-art detectors used in nuclear structure studies for environmental monitoring and emergency preparedness. The Division of Particle and Nuclear Physics, which has approximately 50 employees, conducts a broad range of research in both theoretical and experimental particle and heavy-ion physics, as well as experimental nuclear physics. The Nuclear Structure Group is active in several international collaborations exploiting large-scale accelerator facilities across the globe. With the present position, however, we thrive to intensify local collaborations with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group. Being a doctoral student As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree. More about being a doctoral student at the Science Faculty . Project Description The project "From Lundium to L.U.N.D.I.U.M." (Swedish Radiation Safety Authority) will see the upcycling of various state-of-the-art components of the Lundium decay station for studies of Super Heavy Elements into L.U.N.D.I.U.M.: the Lund University Next-generation Device for Identification of Unknown radioactive sources and environmental Monitoring. L.U.N.D.I.U.M. will have unprecedented alpha-beta-gamma resolving capabilities stemming from its high granularity of detector components and contemporary multi-coincidence data acquisition systems. The research environment constitutes an interdisciplinary community of knowledge and practice focused on data analysis and simulations of complex datasets to be used for radiation safety and emergency preparedness within the disciplines of physics, work environment, medical radiation physics, and environmental monitoring. We are now recruiting one PhD student to be integrated into the research group and lead this development from conceptualization and optimization via Monte Carlo Geant4 simulations to realization of the device. The PhD student will collaborate during specific phases of their doctoral education, with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group for sample collection and preparation. Work duties You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences. The PhD project will address the need for expanding the Swedish network of environmental monitor and emergency preparedness with the development and usage of a new-generation device for nuclear forensics. The tasks include: Optimize via Monte Carlo simulations the geometry and elements of the new device upcycling the existing state-of-the-art detector components for measurement of various types of environmental filter and electroplated samples. Conduct and coordinate the mechanical construction of the device and develop its data acquisition system and data analysis framework. Validation of the measurements using simulated contamination samples provided by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) for yearly proficiency tests. In close collaboration with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group, develop methods to analyse radioactive aerosols from environmental samples. At various stages of the project, close collaboration is envisaged with researchers at the University of Jyväskylä, Finland, in charge of a comparable measurement station. The research projects will be reported in the form of articles submitted for publication in scientific journals, reports to the funding organisation, and conference contributions. The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (up to a maximum of 20% of working time). Qualifications To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below. Specific admission requirements A person meets the specific admission requirements for third-cycle programme in Physics, if they: has at least 45 second cycle credits in physics or engineering physics or an associated field, or has a second cycle (master) degree in physics or engineering physics or an associated field. The specific entry requirement may also have been obtained through other equivalent education, which is assessed in each individual case. Finally, the student must be judged to have the potential to complete the programme. Additional requirements In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: completion of courses amounting to at least 60 credits that are directly relevant to the PhD education a strong ability to work independently and the ability to formulate and address scientific problems good written and oral communication skills good ability to collaborate very good proficiency in English, both spoken and written an interest in interdisciplinary work Other qualifications (advantages) For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications: excellent laboratory skills concerning contemporary radiation detectors proficiency with multi-parameter data acquisition systems proficiency in modern object oriented programming knowledge of environmental radioactivity or radioecology knowledge of radionuclide production in nuclear power plants and spallation sources previous experience to ionizing radiation detection previous experience with Monte Carlo radiation transport codes We offer Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. It is advisable to enter information on what your unit specifically can offer as a workplace. More information about working at Lund University on lu.se . About the employment The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting 1 January 2027 at the earliest. Third cycle studies consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§. More information about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages . Other Selection for admission to doctoral studies is based on the assessed ability to successfully complete the doctoral education. The assessment of this ability is primarily based on study results at the first- and second-cycle (Bachelor’s and Master’s) levels. The following criteria will be considered: Knowledge and skills relevant to the doctoral project and the field of study, as described under Work duties . These may be demonstrated through submitted documentation. Assessed ability to work independently and to formulate and address scientific problems. This assessment may, for example, be based on the degree project and a discussion thereof during a potential interview. Ability to communicate effectively in writing and orally. Other experience relevant to doctoral studies, such as professional experience. Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, initiative, independence, and personal suitability, as well as to how the applicant’s experience and competence are assessed to demonstrate the ability required to complete the doctoral education. How to apply Applications shall be written in English and include: CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background. Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project. Other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.) We welcome your application! No Offer Description Introduction to the vacant position: The Microenvironments for Medicine Group is seeking a PhD student to develop in vitro models of the oesophageal epithelium and investigate the role of cell and matrix mechanics in cancer initiation. The position is funded by a project from the Fundación Científica Asociación Española Contra el Cáncer, and will be developed in collaboration with Dr Albert Herms (IDIBAPS). The work involves engineering viscoelastic hydrogels to support epithelial cell growth and characterising them using mechanobiology techniques, including Brillouin microscopy and traction force microscopy. Main tasks and responsibilities: Establishing a toolset for understanding cancer initiation in the esophageous involving mechanical, chemical and computational techniques. These will include: Chemical synthesis of novel viscoelastic hydrogels Advanced rheological characterization both at the micro and the bulk scale Cell culture Cellular and molecular biology techniques Advanced live microscopy experiments, including Brillouin Microscopy Advanced characterisation of cell mechanics Requirements for candidates: Essential: Degree and Master on any field on physics, biology, engineering, Multidisciplinary qualifications (Physics/Maths, Physics/Engineering, etc.) and/or knowledge on hydrogels, cell biology (specifically on advanced microscopy techniques will be a plus). Competencies and skills: Communication, Teamwork and collaboration, Commitment, Proactivity, Integrity, Critical and Analytical thinking. High level of English. Candidates must not yet have been awarded a doctoral degree. Advantageous: Experience in computational modelling of biological systems Experience with immune and mesenchymal stem cells We Offer: Number of available positions: 1 Starting date: flexible from 1st January 2027 Working conditions: Full time 4-year contract. Measures to reconcile work and family life (parental leave, flexible schedule working hours, 23 working days of paid holidays, 9 leave days for personal matters, among others). IBEC ensures equality of access to professional development opportunities irrespective of employment status, length at IBEC or other factors. The IBEC’s yearly training catalogue offers a wide range of training in technical and transferable skills including mobility grants and a Mentoring programme for predoctoral and postdoctoral researchers. Stimulating, interdisciplinary research and high-quality international scientific environment. Induction programme to facilitate incorporation at IBEC and additional support is provided for foreigners to obtain Visa-working permit and to install in Barcelona. No Offer Description About the workplace The Molecular Neuroanatomy research group, led by Åsa Mackenzie, investigates the organisation and function of the brain in Parkinson’s disease. Using anatomical, molecular and functional approaches, we study brain regions and neural circuits involved in both motor and non-motor symptoms, with a particular focus on the subthalamic region and its relevance to deep brain stimulation (DBS). Our research combines neuroanatomical studies of human and animal brain tissue with experimental studies in mice. We use histological and molecular methods, together with functional techniques, to advance our understanding of the neural circuits affected in Parkinson’s disease. The research group is currently expanding and comprises the principal investigator, a project and data manager, researchers and students. We are now looking for a committed and experienced Laboratory Research Assistant to become an important part of our experimental research activities. We are looking for someone with a genuine interest in hands-on laboratory work, who enjoys experimental tasks and is motivated to contribute actively to the development and maintenance of a well-organised and efficiently functioning laboratory. The project is supported by the Aligning Science Across Parkinson’s (ASAP) Collaborative Research Network (CRN), an international research initiative dedicated to accelerating discoveries in Parkinson’s disease through scientific collaboration, resource development and data sharing We offer a stimulating research environment where you will work closely with researchers and students and contribute to research addressing important questions in Parkinson’s disease. The research is conducted at the Biomedical Centre (BMC), located close to Skåne University Hospital in Lund, Sweden. Within our research group, we are committed to maintaining a positive working environment characterised by mutual respect, consideration and collaboration. We strive to create an inclusive workplace where all team members have opportunities for professional development, participation and job satisfaction. What we offer As a public-sector employer, Lund University offers a range of employment benefits, including generous annual leave and a favourable occupational pension scheme. We also offer flexible working hours, providing good opportunities to maintain a healthy work–life balance. Read more about the benefits of working at Lund University: Working at Lund University. Work duties and responsibilities The position is primarily laboratory-based and involves active participation in the day-to-day experimental work of the laboratory. Duties include, but are not limited to: Tissue sectioning using a cryostat and/or microtome. Histological techniques, including in situ hybridisation, immunohistochemistry and various histological staining methods. PCR analyses of tissue samples. Assisting with stereotactic brain surgery in mice for optogenetic studies. Tract tracing and behavioural analyses in mice. Over time, the position may also involve certain administrative responsibilities, such as chemical management and registration in KLARA and purchasing through Procedo. Other duties may also be assigned. We are looking for someone who enjoys hands-on experimental work, has excellent practical skills and takes responsibility for carrying out tasks accurately and systematically. Contributing to good laboratory organisation, established routines and a well-functioning laboratory environment is an important part of the role. Qualifications Required qualifications A completed university degree (excluding professional/vocational degrees) that included practical laboratory work and experimental training in molecular biology and/or histology. Previous experience in neurobiological research. Good practical experience in tissue sectioning using a cryostat and/or microtome, as well as in histological techniques. Experience of working in accordance with good laboratory practice, including careful documentation and maintaining an organised laboratory environment. FELASA-accredited training or equivalent qualifications for working with laboratory mice. Good ability to work independently as well as collaboratively, follow instructions, and report results both verbally and in writing. Great emphasis will be placed on personal qualities. We are looking for someone who is meticulous, organised, reliable and responsible, with good interpersonal skills and a positive approach to their work. Desirable qualifications Education specialising in molecular biology, histology or neuroscience. Good knowledge of brain anatomy and function. Practical experience of one or more of the following techniques: PCR-based genotyping, in situ hybridisation, immunohistochemistry, optogenetics and behavioural analyses in mice. Experience in stereotactic surgery, viral vector delivery and/or tract tracing. Excellent practical skills and a genuine interest in hands-on laboratory and experimental work. Willingness and ability to take responsibility for the laboratory’s daily routines, maintain good organisation and contribute to a well-functioning laboratory environment. Other information The position is a fixed-term employment according to the Special Fixed-term Employment (SÄVA) regulations §5 p1 LAS, and it is full-time. The desired start date is 2027-01-11 or as agreed upon, with an end date of 2028-01-10. How to Apply Applications are to be submitted via the University’s recruitment system. The application should include a CV and a personal letter justifying your interest in the position and how it matches your qualifications. The application should also include a degree certificate or equivalent and any other document to which you would like to draw attention (copies of grade transcripts, details of referees, letters of recommendation, etc.). The Department of Clinical Sciences, Lund, is one of six departments within the Faculty of Medicine at Lund University. The Department has extensive collaborations both within the Faculty and with other parts of the University. It also has well-established collaborations with Skåne University Hospital, Region Skåne, the wider community and the business sector. These collaborations help promote clinical and experimental translational research, development and education. We warmly welcome your application! No Offer Description Your Field of Activity: A historically oriented anthropology of song traditions will engage with pāṭṭu by combining text critical analyses of written sources with studying of actual performances in an integrative approach. Our modus operandi will follow the logic of combined “deep reading” sensitive to “sensorial epistemology”: sustained, intense, and probing engagement with texts, whether literary, musical, graphic, dramatic, or theoretical. This approach will be enriched by a focus on sensorial epistemologies, aesthetic dimensions of material culture, and oral, written, and embodied protocols of creation and reception. VOICES proposes a new analytical tool made of a set of five mutually dependent research clusters (RC). These are organized around the idea of different modes (“bodies”) of meaning-making through singing which we identify as shared by majority of the song traditions addressed by the project. In keeping with the focus on the socio-cultural aspects of the singing body referred to above, and the project’s marked historical perspective, each of the clusters is guided by a set of research questions emerging from our pilot studies of the singing cultures of South India. You will contribute to two main research clusters: Cluster 1 studies how songs tie social bonds and historically imagine collective identities by reframing epic, mythic and individual imaginaries. Source texts in original language like Payyannūrppāṭṭu , Rāmacaritam; Vaṭakkanpāṭṭu, Ceruśśeri’s Kṛṣṇagātha-pāṭṭu, Eḻuttacchan’s Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa and Mahābhāratamkiḷipāṭṭus. Performances such as: Paṭayani; Brāhmaṇipāṭṭu Cluster 2 explores how songs of war, resistance and subversion, mobilize and channel collective emotions and become medium for either support or discord and dissension. Source Texts in original language like cāvēṟŭpāṭṭu, tampuranpāṭṭu ; Eḻuttacchan’s Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa and Mahābhāratam , Kuñcan Nampyar’s Pātracaritam kilippāṭṭu ; pātappāṭṭu ; taccōlippāṭṭu. Collaborate with our digital humanities team to engage actively in the development of the “Mapping Sonic Ecumene: A Visual Archive of Sound”. This involves mapping and archiving sonic and visual representations of songs across South India, contributing to the design process, refining content, and regularly updating our online platforms with accessible, well-documented findings. Collaborate closely with the VOICES team, including contributing to the planning and development of events, workshops. description: 24 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Inria, the French national research institute for the digital sciences Research Field Computer science Researcher Profile Recognised Researcher (R2) Application Deadline 22 Nov 2026 - 00:00 (UTC) Country France Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Hours Per Week 38.5 Offer Starting Date 4 Jan 2027 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? No Offer Description Deep learning has transformed protein structure prediction. However, current models can still produce physically implausible structures with high confidence. These failures, known as hallucinations , remain poorly understood and raise fundamental questions about the reliability, interpretability, and limitations of protein language models (pLMs). This project aims to systematically characterize these failures and develop methods to understand and anticipate them. It builds on FLoPS, a dataset of hallucinated protein language model predictions, with physically grounded quality annotations generated using the abstraqt method. These annotations provide residue- and contact-level information, going beyond conventional metrics based on comparisons with reference structures. The project comprises two complementary research directions: Model interpretability and explainability: identify sequence features, attention mechanisms, and internal representations associated with hallucinations, with the goal of understanding why models generate physically implausible structures. Generative protein structure modelling: depending on the candidate’s interests and expertise, contribute to the development of a novel flow-matching architecture for protein structure prediction, aiming to reduce reliance on evolutionary information and incorporate physically motivated mechanisms of structural formation. Main objectives Develop a systematic explainability methodology for protein language model failures, grounded in residue- and contact-level physical plausibility annotations. Identify input features, internal mechanisms, and latent representations associated with hallucinations. Investigate whether model failures can be detected or predicted from internal signals and model outputs. Depending on the candidate’s background and scientific interests, contribute to the design of flow-matching-based generative protein structure predictors that rely less heavily on evolutionary information. The position is based at Inria Sophia Antipolis on the French Riviera, within an interdisciplinary research environment at the intersection of machine learning, bioinformatics, and biophysics. The successful candidate will have access to local computing resources and Grid’5000, the French national testbed for experimental research in distributed computing and high-performance computing. Position highlights: an emerging research topic with strong scientific potential, access to physically annotated data, opportunities to develop novel explainability methods for large neural networks, and the possibility of contributing to generative protein structure modelling. The successful candidate will primarily lead the research track devoted to explaining hallucinations in protein language models. They will design and implement analytical methods that link model-internal mechanisms to the physical quality of predicted structures, using the FLoPS dataset and the annotations generated by abstraqt. They will define experimental protocols, conduct quantitative and qualitative analyses, assess the robustness of the proposed methods, and contribute to the scientific interpretation of the results. Particular attention will be paid to relationships between input sequence properties, model activations and attention mechanisms, latent representations, and the different failure modes observed. The successful candidate will oversee the scientific and technical development of their research, from experimental design to dissemination. They will contribute to scientific publications and the dissemination of methods and results, including the development of reproducible code. Depending on their expertise and interests, they may also contribute, on an exploratory basis, to the project’s second research track: the development of flow-matching-based protein structure predictors, in collaboration with researchers working on generative modelling and molecular simulation. Collaboration and responsibilities Collaborate with the research team on the development, analysis, and exploitation of the FLoPS dataset. Develop and benchmark explainability methods tailored to protein language models and physical plausibility annotations. Design rigorous and reproducible evaluation protocols to identify mechanisms associated with hallucinations. Contribute to interdisciplinary scientific discussions at the intersection of machine learning, bioinformatics, and biophysics. Depending on expertise and project needs, contribute to methodological developments in flow matching and protein structure prediction. Disseminate research outcomes through scientific publications, presentations, and, where possible, the sharing of reproducible code and resources. References [1] E. Sarti and F. description: Job vacancy PhD Candidate (MSCA) in optimal high temperature heat pump control About the position SINTEF Energy is announcing two PhD candidate positions within the field of thermal engineering and industrial heat supply utilizing High Temperature Heat Pumps (HTHPs). Both positions are within the frame of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN). The candidate will be employed by the Energy Use Department to carry out the doctoral project described below, enrolled by the doctoral program at Brunel University (UK), and have supervisors at both SINTEF and Brunel. About the project The activity is coordinated within the HeatMinds MSCA-DN by Brunel University in London, UK. The HeatMinds project is officially launched in October 2026 and holds a consortium of 18 partners across Europe. This integrated project aims to conduct collaborative research while training fifteen doctoral candidates to make a step change in accelerating the development and deployment of industrial HTHPs to support the decarbonization of heat supply in the process industry. Supported by leading universities, research centres, and industrial actors, advanced models and design tools will be developed that contribute to the advancement of these efforts. HeatMinds will tackle highly connected research questions, namely what are the optimum and sustainable cycle arrangements, component designs, and supporting energy policy frameworks? HeatMinds will establish a roadmap for deploying IHTHP technology to support the decarbonisation of several key industries. The other project partners recruiting PhD students are Brunel University (UK), City St. Georges University (UK), University of Seville (Spain), Technical University of Denmark, and SINTEF Industry. One of the PhD projects hosted by SINTEF Energy is titled “Advanced Control Strategies for Dynamic Operation of High-Temperature Heat Pump Systems”. The project will address the challenges related to optimal control of high temperature heat pumps and their integration within dynamic industrial processes. This project includes elements of: Investigation and development of novel or advanced control algorithms such as model predictive control (MPC) and reinforcement learning (RL) for high-temperature heat pump systems. Investigation and development of control strategies for high-temperature heat pump systems that achieve near-optimal operation using simple control elements (self-optimizing control). Evaluation of proposed control strategies in integrated scenarios within the context of industrial decarbonization and energy system flexibility. Demonstration and evaluation of proposed control strategies in a pilot-scale laboratory system. SINTEF Energy, along with the partners in HeatMinds, hold significant experience and expertise in the analysis, design, and experimental testing of high temperature heat pumps, as well as advanced control methodologies for energy systems. Brunel University additionally has an extensive track record working with control strategies and algorithms. The work will be conducted in close collaboration with SINTEF colleagues as well as with HeatMinds partners. The project includes an international secondment to the German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Low Carbon Industrial Processes to gain practical insight into high temperature heat pump control methods realized in modern experimental facilities. Duties of the position Publish scientific articles and contribute to dissemination activities. Engage in collaboration and secondment with HeatMinds partners. Participate in relevant conferences, workshops, and training activities. Be flexible and prepare to adjust to activities and project focus as the PhD project progresses if needed. Complete the doctoral education. Participate actively in the relevant SINTEF Energy research groups’ activities. Required selection criteria You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree[JD1.1]. Master’s students in their final year can apply, but the degree must be completed and documented before 1 January 2027. Strong academic record (average grade B or better) or demonstrated research potential Must meet the admission requirements for the Mechanical Engineering PhD program at Brunel University. Excellent written and spoken English. MSCA Mobility Rule: At the time of employment, the candidate must not have lived, worked, or studied in Norway for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date of the position. The appointment is to be made in accordance with SINTEF’s guidelines for recruitment positions and the academic regulations set by Brunel University. Background (mandatory) Mathematical modeling, simulation, and analysis of dynamic thermal systems Thermodynamic cycle analysis Control theory and PID controller tuning Proficiency in scientific programming (MATLAB/Python) Additional background that will be valued in the selection process: Advanced control algorithms including MPC and/or RL Heat pump and/or thermal management system analysis and design Familiarity with optimisation methods (e.g. gradient-based methods) Familiarity with plantwide control procedures (e.g. self-optimizing control) Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently and take initiative. Plan and carry out research systematically. Collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Show strong motivation and curiosity for the subject. Communicate clearly and constructively with colleagues. Emphasis will be placed on personal suitability and motivation for the position. We offer An exciting and challenging research project within an international MSCA Doctoral Network With excellent opportunities to collaborate within international research groups and industry. A dynamic, creative, and inclusive working environment. Access to cutting edge facilities and interdisciplinary training. Career development and mentoring through the HeatMinds network. Salary and conditions The employment period is three years, funded through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network Grant HeatMinds. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. About the application The application must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter). Curriculum vitae. Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale. Names and contact information of two references. No Offer Description Oslo University Hospital invites applications for a full-time, two-year Researcher position within SYNAPSE, a project funded by the Research Council of Norway. We seek a researcher with a strong background in computer networking and experience developing or applying machine-learning methods to networking problems. Both positions are within the framework of an MSCA Doctoral Network. The candidate will be employed by the Energy Use Department to carry out the doctoral project described below, enrolled in the doctoral programme at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), and supervised by researchers at both SINTEF and DTU Construct. Launched in October 2026, HeatMinds comprises a consortium of 18 partners across Europe and aims to conduct collaborative research while training fifteen doctoral candidates. The project seeks to accelerate the development and deployment of industrial high-temperature heat pumps to support the decarbonisation of heat supply in the process industry. Supported by leading universities, research centres and industrial actors, HeatMinds will develop advanced models and design tools addressing optimal and sustainable cycle arrangements, component designs and supporting energy policy frameworks.
