No Offer Description The PhD student recruited will work within a team comprising seven permanent staff members. This team is part of the MCD unit. The MCD unit focuses on fundamental research in the life sciences, centring on the mechanisms governing the organisation and function of genomes, cell division and cell mechanics, cell identity and development. The MCD unit comprises 26 teams, organising the work of over 200 people across four research programmes. Ribosomes are the only molecular machines capable of synthesising proteins. Their synthesis is therefore crucial for the cell, which devotes a very significant proportion of its resources to this process. This synthesis is activated under conditions of increased demand for protein synthesis, particularly in cancers. Ribosomes consist of two subunits, a large (60S) and a small (40S) subunit, each composed of one or more ribosomal RNA (rRNA) molecules associated with numerous ribosomal proteins (RPs). The catalytic activity of ribosomes—namely, the synthesis of peptide bonds—is mediated by rRNA. This activity depends on the correct synthesis of rRNA molecules and their proper assembly with their partner RP proteins. rRNA molecules are produced from precursor molecules (pre-rRNAs), which contain additional sequences ('spacer' sequences) absent from mature rRNAs and which are progressively removed during the maturation of the pre-rRNAs. These will also undergo post-transcriptional modifications of specific nucleotides and be folded very gradually whilst associating with RPs in a specific order. These stages of maturation and assembly take place within precursor particles known as 'pre-ribosomal' particles. In addition to pre-rRNA molecules at various stages of maturation and RPs, these pre-ribosomal particles contain, at an early stage, hundreds of small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein particles (snoRNPs), as well as so-called maturation and assembly factors (AFs). snoRNPs and AFs interact with the pre-ribosomal particles and are involved, directly or indirectly, in the nucleotide modifications of pre-rRNAs, the removal of spacer sequences, the secondary and tertiary folding of pre-rRNAs, and the insertion of RPs. The majority of AFs involved in the synthesis of eukaryotic ribosomes have been identified. Many of these factors are enzymes such as helicases, kinases, GTPases, ATPases, endo- and exonucleases, methyltransferases, etc. In many cases, their substrates and precise molecular roles in ribosome synthesis remain unknown. The thesis topic concerns the early stages of assembly and maturation of pre-ribosomal particles that are precursors to the large ribosomal subunit. These stages are among the least understood aspects of eukaryotic ribosome synthesis. This is partly due to the fact that far fewer structural data are available for the corresponding pre-ribosomal particles. Indeed, atomic-scale structures of later-stage pre-ribosomal particles have been obtained using cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), enabling hypotheses regarding the mode of action of the snoRNPs and AFs they contain to be proposed and tested. No complete atomic structures are available for very early pre-ribosomal particles in the synthesis pathway of the large subunit. It is nevertheless known that these early particles contain dozens of snoRNPs and AFs, notably RNA helicases that could remodel rRNA structures or rRNA/protein interactions, and snoRNPs in complex with AFs. The aim of the PhD project will be to elucidate, in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the precise molecular functions in the synthesis of the large ribosomal subunit of a molecular machine consisting of a snoRNP containing the C/D-box small RNA snR190, associated with a complex of five assembly factors—known as the Npa1 complex—comprising the proteins Npa1, Npa2, Nop8, Rsa3 and the DEAD-box RNA helicase Dbp6. The studies will also be extended to investigate the roles of the homologues of these factors in human cells, where the formation of this molecular machine has yet to be demonstrated. In yeast, we have shown that this molecular machine is required for the early stages of large subunit synthesis. The aim of the PhD project will be to determine the role of this machine in the assembly of pre-ribosomal particles (i.e. the integration of RPs, AFs and snoRNPs) using quantitative mass spectrometry, in the folding of early pre-rRNA molecules using the SHAPEmap technique, and in the modification and maturation of pre-rRNA molecules using high-throughput approaches and nanopore RNA sequencing. At the same time, we will determine the structure of the yeast molecular machinery using cryo-ME, either in isolation or embedded within pre-ribosomal particles. These structures will enable us to design targeted mutations within the molecular machine that inhibit certain key interactions, in order to determine their functional consequences using the approaches listed above. Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Turn complex research challenges into IT solutions that move science forward. At Wageningen University & Research (WUR), researchers push boundaries in Food, Nature and Agriculture. They rely on advanced IT to explore new ideas, work with complex data and develop solutions for real-world challenges. As a Senior Research Engineer, you help make that possible. You bring research questions and technology together. Working directly with researchers and IT specialists, you explore what is needed, identify the right technical approach and turn it into a working solution. You combine broad technical expertise with a practical mindset, taking ownership from the first conversation to implementation and delivery. Your work spans software engineering, infrastructure, data platforms and architecture. You make thoughtful technical choices and ensure that solutions are secure, scalable, maintainable and aligned with WUR’s wider IT landscape. You also help researchers understand what technology can do for their work and where its limitations lie. It is an opportunity to make a direct technical contribution to research while helping build the IT capabilities that enable new discoveries. Your team You will join the Research Engineering team within WUR’s Digitalisation, Information and Archiving Services Department, which brings together more than 300 professionals. Our team currently consists of five professionals and is growing. We work closely with research groups and projects across WUR, tackling a wide variety of technical challenges. One project might involve connecting sensors and measuring devices to WUR infrastructure. Another might require integrating scientific applications with shared platforms, processing large volumes of research data or developing infrastructure for AI and scientific computing. To make this happen, we work across cloud environments, Kubernetes clusters, high-performance computing, software, databases and data platforms. You will collaborate with researchers and specialists from across IT, contribute your own expertise and help colleagues find solutions to complex technical problems. What you will do You turn research needs into reliable, practical IT solutions. You combine hands-on engineering with technical leadership and act as a trusted partner to researchers and IT colleagues. Lead complex research IT assignments: take ownership from the initial research question through technical design, implementation and delivery. Explore and translate research needs: work with researchers to understand their processes and challenges, then identify opportunities for integration, automation and improvement. Design and build robust solutions: develop applications, databases, infrastructure and integrations that are secure, scalable and maintainable. Guide technical decisions: assess architectural options, explain trade-offs and align solutions with WUR requirements for architecture, security, privacy and data management. Connect technologies and capabilities: integrate scientific applications, sensors and research tools with WUR infrastructure, and help enable data-intensive research, AI, IoT and scientific computing. Strengthen the team and the wider IT landscape: act as a technical sparring partner, coordinate with relevant specialists, share knowledge and identify opportunities to reuse and standardise solutions. You will help researchers make better use of technology while ensuring that individual solutions contribute to a reliable, sustainable IT landscape across WUR. By combining curiosity, technical expertise and collaboration, you help create the conditions for research to go further. Where to apply Website https://www.academictransfer.com/en/jobs/365207/senior-research-engineer/apply/ Requirements Specific Requirements What we are looking for You are an experienced engineer who enjoys solving complex technical problems and applying technology to real-world research challenges. You are comfortable working independently, taking ownership of solutions and operating across the boundaries of software, infrastructure and research. What you bring You are an experienced engineer who enjoys tackling complex technical challenges and turning research needs into practical IT solutions. You take ownership, work independently and connect the worlds of software, infrastructure and research. You bring: A relevant technical background: a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Engineering, Physics, Mathematics or a related technical or scientific discipline, combined with several years of experience in software engineering, infrastructure engineering, research engineering, technical consulting or a similar role. Experience in a research environment is an advantage. Broad technical expertise: strong software engineering skills, experience with programming and scientific software, and a good understanding of software architecture, infrastructure, security, privacy and data management. Experience with modern infrastructure: knowledge of large-scale computing environments, such as HPC, clusters and cloud platforms, as well as experience with Kubernetes and modern infrastructure and deployment practices. A practical, analytical mindset: the ability to untangle complex technical challenges, make sound technical choices and develop secure, sustainable solutions. You can explain your approach and its trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. A collaborative approach: experience working in Agile environments and multidisciplinary teams, with strong communication and consulting skills. You enjoy working with researchers, engineers, architects and IT specialists to find solutions together. Curiosity and adaptability: an interest in new technologies and the drive to keep learning. You are comfortable working with evolving requirements and finding a way forward when research questions are not yet fully defined. Experience with scientific research processes is highly valuable. You understand that research evolves as new insights emerge, and you can adapt your approach without losing sight of technical quality and long-term maintainability. Above all, you are curious about both technology and research. You enjoy exploring possibilities, tackling difficult problems and working closely with researchers to turn their ideas into reality. Additional Information Benefits Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment . A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8,3%; excellent pension scheme. description: 6 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Universidade do Minho - ISISE Department ISISE Research Field Engineering » Civil engineering Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Positions Master Positions Application Deadline 23 Nov 2026 - 23:00 (Europe/Lisbon) Country Portugal Type of Contract Not Applicable Job Status Not Applicable Offer Starting Date 9 Nov 2026 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Other EU programme Reference Number NORTE2030-FEDER-01432600 Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description A call is open to award (1) research grant within the R&D Project “EcoBEAM - Desenvolvimento de soluções inovadoras de vigas mistas, com foco na sustentabilidade”, project number 18265, operation code NORTE2030-FEDER-01432600, cofunded by the Northern Regional Program (NORTE 2030), by the Portugal 2030 and by the European Union, in its ERFD component, in the following conditions: RESEARCH FIELD: Civil Engineering or related fields. RECIPIENT CATEGORY: Degree courses: Students enrolled in a PhD. Non-conferring degrees courses: Masters enrolled in non-academic degree courses. CANDIDATES PROFILE / CANDIDATE ADMISSIBILITY REQUIREMENTS Mandatory requirements: In order to apply, the candidates must possess: A Master's degree in the field of Civil Engineering or related fields; Applicants must comply with the eligibility conditions set out in Article 9 of the Research Grant Regulations, No. 950/2019, of 16-12-2019, of FCT I.P.. At the time of the respective hiring, candidates must prove that they are enrolled in one of the following courses: PhD in Civil Engineering, or related fields; In a Course that do not confer an academic degree, in the area or area related to that requested in the tender (e.g.: postgraduate studies, advanced studies, specialized training). Preferential factors: Proven knowledge and experience in Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) applied to materials and structural/building solutions; Experience in using life cycle modelling software, namely SimaPro software and inventory databases (e.g., Ecoinvent); Knowledge of sustainability standards and guidelines in construction, namely EN 15804+A2, ISO 14040, ISO 14044 standards, and Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs); Portuguese language proficiency; English language proficiency. Requirement for granting the fellowship: The applicants may apply without prior registration in the course for which the fellowship is open. The requirement to enroll in a degree course or non-academic degree course will be verified on the date of contracting the fellowship. Only fellowships whose selected applicants present a valid proof of enrollment in a degree course or non-academic degree course will be contracted, issued by a Higher Education Institution, according to the type of the fellowship, indicating the academic year or its duration (start and term). APPLICATION / ADMISSIBILITY REQUIREMENTS The call is open from 09/11/2026 to 23/11/2026 (23:00 – Europe/Lisbon). Applications must be sent exclusively by e-mail to isabelv@civil.uminho.pt , with the subject “Edital BI-ISISE-UMINHO-ECOBEAM-18265-B3”, with the following documents: Elements of the National Identity Card/Citizen Card/Passport/Visa/Title of Residence; Curriculum Vitae of the candidate, in Portuguese or in English; Certificates of the academic degree(s) required, specifying the final grading (mandatory) and, if possible, the grades obtained in all the attended curricular units, or, alternatively, the candidate's declaration of honor that the degree was obtained until the end of the term of application (Annex I); Certificate of recognition of foreign academic degree and conversion of the respective final grading into the Portuguese grading scale, or, alternatively, the candidate's declaration of honor (Annex II), if applicable; Statement proving that meets the conditions for the grant typology, according to the application requirements (Annex III); Motivation letter, in Portuguese or in English. Failure to comply with the deadline for submitting the application, such as failure to submit or late submission of the application and the documents referred to in points 2) to 4), determines the exclusion of the application. Regarding the above mentioned admissibility requirements, the following should be noted: In the case of a degree granted by a foreign higher education institution, and in order to ensure the application of the principle of equal treatment to candidates holding foreign and national academic degrees, it is mandatory to recognize the degree and convert the respective final grading to the Portuguese grading scale. The academic degrees and diplomas documents, or their respective recognition when awarded by foreign higher education institutions are not mandatory in the application phase, being replaced by a declaration of honor of the candidate with the contents of academic results. The documents of academic qualification or respective recognition will be required in the contracting phase and must attest facts that occurred on a date prior to the application. In situations of divergence between the information contained in the declaration and the documentation submitted for contracting the grant, only the information contained in the latter will be consider. If the documents proving the ownership of the academic degree and diploma, or the respective recognition under the terms of Decree-Law No. 66/2018, of August 16, do not correspond to the classifications awarded in the evaluation of the academic path, which can change the candidate's ranking, the fellowship won’t be contracted. Applicants with degrees obtained abroad must present proof of recognition of qualifications in Portugal and conversion of the final classification obtained in them to the Portuguese classification scale or declaration under the terms indicated in the previous point. Candidates who do not comply with one of these provisions, the Selection Panel will assign “0” in the respective criteria. Candidates will be evaluated on the remaining parameters. Only candidates who have completed the required qualification by the end of the application period will be admitted. If they do not yet have the official degree certificate, a declaration of honor from the candidate stating that he/she has completed the qualifications required by the end of the application period, will be accepted. At the time of the respective hiring the candidate must present the official degree certificate. DURATION OF THE RESEARCH GRANT The research grant will last for 12 months, with a provisional starting date in January 2027. The grant may be renewed until the maximum predicted in the project and/or applicable legislation, if it is necessary to complete the academic degree or to carry out activities that are essential for the conclusion of the project. If the grant is awarded to candidates enrolled in a course that does not confer an academic degree, the grant cannot be renewed. WORK PLAN AND OBJECTIVES The work plan is intended to contribute to the objectives of Activity 4 (Life Cycle Assessment), specifically Task 4.1 (Definition of the life cycle assessment database) and Task 4.2 (Life cycle assessment of the construction solutions involved in the project), namely: Survey and definition of life cycle inventory (LCI) data and respective environmental performance for the components and innovative structural solutions of the project; Development and structuring of a life cycle inventory database guided by the methodology recommended by standard EN 15804+A2 and applicable Product Category Rules (PCRs); Life cycle modelling of systems and input/output flows (from raw material extraction to end-of-life) following a cradle-to-cradle approach (ISO 14040 and ISO 14044), using SimaPro modelling software and the Ecoinvent database; Execution of the Life Cycle Cost Analysis (LCC) for the different scenarios of the innovative structural system in accordance with standard ISO 15686-5 and SETAC guidelines; Performance of a comparative analysis between all proposed innovative alternatives and reference structural solutions (e.g., reinforced concrete and steel); Structuring the database with contents and formatting compatible with Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) to support project teams and the preparation of respective project scientific deliverables and reports. The work plan includes the support to the execution of the project deliverables, including scientific publications and periodic reports. HOST INSTITUTION AND SCIENTIFIC SUPERVISION The work will be carried out at ISISE - Institute for Sustainability and Innovation in Structural Engineering - Civil Engineering Department, School of Engineering of the University of Minho, located at Azurém (Guimarães), under the scientific supervision of Doctor Ricardo Filipe Mesquita da Silva Mateus and Doctor Maria Isabel Brito Valente and coordination of Doctor José Manuel Sena Cruz. EVALUATION CRITERIA The evaluation of the applications will focus on the Merit of the Candidate, by applying the following criteria on a scale of 0 to 5 points: Candidate's Merit – CM (100%): Criterion A - Motivation Letter – 15%; Criterion B - Academic performance (Final classification of the Master's Degree) – 50%; Criterion C - Personal Curriculum (reflecting scientific and professional background) – 35%: Sub‑criterion C1 - Professional or academic experience in Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and modelling using SimaPro software applied to construction materials or products – 85% Sub‑criterion C2 - Publications in journals and conferences relevant to the project theme (LCA, sustainability, materials, and structures) – 15% The final classification of the Candidate’s Merit (CM) will be obtained by applying the following formula: CM = (A*0,15) + (B*0,50) + (0,35*((C1*0,85) + (C2*0,15))) Candidates with a final MC score lower than 3.0 points are immediately excluded from the selection process. The jury may choose to conduct an interview. In this case, the top 3 candidates ranked on the MC ordered list will be selected for the interview. Interview – INT (40%): Criterion E1 - Motivation, with a weighting of 30%; Criterion E2 - Technical knowledge necessary for the execution of the work plan, with a weighting of 30%; Criterion E3 - Overall assessment, with a weighting of 40%. The Interview score (INT) will be calculated using the following formula: INT = (E1*0,30) + (E2*0,30) + (E3*0,40) The final classification (FC) combining the Candidate Merit (CM) and the Interview (INT) will be calculated using the following formula: FC = (CM*0,60) + (INT*0,40) The Selection Committee reserves the right not to award the research scholarship in this call, based on the results of the candidate evaluation and their suitability for the project’s objectives. SELECTION PANEL The Selection Panel is composed by the following elements: President: Doctor Maria Isabel Brito Valente, Assistant Professor of the Civil Engineering Department, ISISE, School of Engineering, University of Minho. Effective members: Doctor João Miguel Pereira, Assistant Researcher, ISISE, School of Engineering, University of Minho, and Doctor Ricardo Filipe Mesquita da Silva Mateus, Associate Professor of the Civil Engineering Department, ISISE, School of Engineering, University of Minho. Substitute members: Doctor José Manuel de Sena Cruz, Associate Professor with Habilitation of the Civil Engineering Department, ISISE, School of Engineering, University of Minho, and Doctor Miguel Ângelo Dias Azenha, Associate Professor with Habilitation of the Civil Engineering Department, ISISE, School of Engineering, University of Minho. If the President of the Selection Panel is unavailable, he/she shall be replaced by the first effective member. The first substitute member will replace the effective member. The Selection Panel, including the President, undertake the commitment to respect a set of responsibilities essential to the evaluation process, such as the duties of impartiality, of stating any potential situations of conflict of interest and confidentiality. COMUNICATION OF RESULTS The results of the evaluation are announced by email to all candidates, attaching, for this purpose, the minutes of the jury's deliberations, within a maximum period of 60 working days from the deadline for submission of applications. Candidates are informed, at a preliminary hearing, in accordance with Articles 121 and 122 of the Administrative Procedure Code (DL nº 4 / 2015 of January 7), of the likely outcome of the final decision, and may comment within 10 working days of this notification. COMPLAINT AND APPEAL PROCEDURES The selected candidate must indicate, in writing, the intention to accept the grant, within 10 working days of notification of the grant award. The final decision can be contested, having 15 working days for this purpose, or an appeal may be lodged with the Rector within 30 working days, both after the respective notification. REQUIREMENTS FOR FINAL AWARDING OF THE GRANT The scholarship is awarded through the signing of a contract between the University of Minho and the scholarship recipient, in accordance with the draft contract in Annex II of the University of Minho Regulations (RBIC).At the time of hiring, the following documents must be sent: National Identity Card/Citizen Card/Passport/Visa/Title of Residence; Copy of the certificate of the academic degree; Presentation of the certificate of recognition of foreign academic degree and conversion of the respective final grading into the Portuguese grading scale, if applicable; Document proving enrollment in the Doctoral Program or in a Course that does not confer an academic degree, identified in this application; Science ID; NIB/IBAN (document of the Bank with the name of the candidate); Tax Identification Number (NIF); Digital mobile key (digital signature). The contract may only be concluded after all the documentation required is collected, which must take place within a maximum period of 6 months.Once all the documentation has been received, the contracting entity has a period of 60 working days to conclude the scholarship contract, in accordance with nº3 of the Article 14º the University of Minho Regulations (RBIC). MONTHLY MAINTENANCE ALLOWANCE The Monthly Maintenance Allowance corresponds to the basic value of 1359.64 euros per month, according to the table of grants of FCT, I.P. in the country ( https://www.fct.pt/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Tabela-de-Valores-SMM-2026.pdf ) and Research Scholarship of the University of Minho, updated annually, as decided by the Management Board. Payments are made by bank transfer on the 23rd of each month to the Bank Identification Number of the fellow identified in the contratualization process. OTHER BENEFITS Reimbursement of the Voluntary Social Insurance, if the candidate chooses to receive it, corresponding to the 1st tier of the contribution base (for grants of 6 months or more) and Personal Accident Insurance. EXCLUSIVITY REGIME The grantee will perform the activities under exclusivity, as foreseen in article 5º of the Research Fellow Statutes and applicable regulations. TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR GRANT RENEWAL Grant may be renewed for additional periods, if this information is provided in “DURATION OF THE RESEARCH GRANT" and in the contract. This additional period may not exceed the regulatory limits or the end of the project. The renewal of the grant always depends on a petition submitted by the grant holder, on a date prior to the end of the grant contract, accompanied by the following documents: report issued by the supervisor(s) and by the host entity(ies) on the follow-up of the grant holder's work and the evaluation of his/her activities; updated document proving compliance with the exclusive dedication regime; document proving the renewal of enrollment in the study cycle leading to an academic
